events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

options.text: Invest in peace with [rival].
Politely decline.

events.text: Emissaries from [rival] return to court. They are eager to restart negotiations. "Are you better positioned now to afford peace with our people?" What is our response?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

options.text: Peace is the path of the wise.
Politely decline.
Now is not the time, but perhaps later...

events.text: A diplomat arrives from faraway [rival]. He toasts the court with a cup of fine wine. "Now that our two peoples have established relations, [character] wishes to know if you would be interested in a formal peace." How shall we reply?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

options.text: Our champion shall bring us victory.
Victory is determined on battlefields, not in arenas.
We offer [rival] a generous gift instead.

events.text: An emissary arrives from [rival], accompanied by a mighty champion. "We seek to pit our finest champion against yours, in a contest to the death. The nation whose champion loses this duel shall owe tribute to the victor." As if to motivate the court, the [rival] champion sits at the head of the chamber and begins to sharpen a bloody sword. Do we dare agree to such an unusual proposition?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

options.text: We shall pay tribute to [rival].
[rival] will never pay for peace.
Let us not forge a peace with favors.
Your wine was poisoned... and peace will be on our terms.

events.text: [rival] emissary arrives with news from his ruler, [character]. Over drinks, he explains his nation's position. "[character] appreciates the respect you have shown to Persia. Grant us tribute, and we will agree to a lasting peace." He finishes his wine, slurping every drop. What shall we say to this offer?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

options.text: If [rival] wishes to test our resolve, so be it.
Beg for mercy and offer to pay tribute.

events.text: An emissary arrives from [rival], unannounced. He brings a startling declaration: [rival] declares war! "Non ducor, duco!" he cries. Our scholars translate his words as, "We are not led, but lead!" All [rival] awaits our response...

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

options.text: Our suggestion was in jest. We desire peace.
Let us forget the past and discuss trade.
No more talk, then. It is time for action.

events.text: The emissary from [rival] stands before you again. "[character] did not appreciate your suggestion that we pay [rival] tribute. You have done nothing but talk, and talk is cheap." What shall we tell [character]?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

tip: As leader: +50 Unit Trait XP / Infantry
As governor: +100 Unit Trait XP / Infantry

options.text: "We didn't want your Tribute anyway. It will be more fun to crush you in battle."

events.text: A dour emissary arrives from [rival]. Wasting no time with pleasantries or formal introductions, she delivers her message from [character], "You push us too far. Now we shall push back."

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

options.text: Arrange deals with our merchants.
The court will invest in new trade routes.

events.text: [rival] dignitary bows before us, issuing a greeting from [character]. "Our ruler is interested in your offer of trade. How can we make this happen?" What deal shall we strike with the [rival]?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Neither, Nor

options.text: Let us bring this affair to an end.

events.text: Our advisors report that the [tribe] match is neither pleasing nor displeasing, crass nor witty, handsome nor plain. Few should have objections to this arrangement, but equally few will be delighted.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Nero's Suspicion

options.text: Surely he wouldn't turn on me.

events.text: Surrounded by people jealous of your grip on power and hold over him, your informants tell you that [character] has started to believe the lies being whispered that you are plotting against him.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: New Alliance

options.text: Success is good, but let us wait before trying this again.
The results speak for themselves. Give him the needed support.

events.text: Scouts bring heartening news from the [tribe] camps. The two men sent by [character] to infiltrate the barbarian leadership have succeeded. The [tribe] have requested a formal Alliance Tribe. Emboldened, [character] requests support for future missions.

events.author: Solver
events.name: New Explorers

options.text: A great journey begins now.

events.text: You have discovered several prominent landmarks, but your desires are far from satisfied. If anything, you have become even more eager to explore the world, seeing how many natural wonders there are close to our cities - who knows what miracles may be found if we stray further away? What [rival] needs is to recruit the bravest and most ambitious explorers who will travel by land or by sea and discover whatever there is to discover. [rival] will be second to only the gods themselves in its knowledge of the world!

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: New Slaves from [city]

options.text: Sell them into slavery.
Use them as slaves in [city].
Slaughter them all for fighting us.

events.text: Following the taking of [city], your troops round up a large number of citizens, dragging them from their hiding places in cellars and warehouses.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: New Type of Animal Discovered

options.text: We will pay well for a new source of gems.
Leave this matter to the locals in [city].

events.text: Years have passed since a new species of spider was found near [city], but its scientists continue to search for discoveries along the local waterways. One of these men claims to have stumbled upon precious stones in his search, but he will not provide more information until he is paid. Do we reward him for his efforts?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: No Evidence

options.text: No, I am tired of jumping at shadows.
If there is a plot, it must be uprooted.

events.text: It appears that your Spymaster's suspicions about the [family] Family were unwarranted. Despite the occasional frustration, they remain loyal to the throne. [character] insists that a plot led by [character] simmers in the court, and he asks for permission to conduct another, more rigorous inquiry.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: No Longer of Use

options.text: If [character] is not careful, he shall shortly learn [rival] is far better an ally than an adversary.

events.text: Perhaps [character] is overconfident. Or perhaps [rival] power has reached a zenith, and ties to the backwater of [rival] now serve only as a risk and distraction.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: No Longer of Use

options.text: If [character] is not careful, he shall shortly learn [rival] is far better an ally than an adversary.

events.text: Perhaps [character] is overconfident. Or perhaps [rival] power has reached a zenith, and ties to the backwater of [rival] now serve only as a risk and distraction.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: No More Delays

options.text: I shall judge these cases myself and judge them fairly. Trials begin within the week.
Assign these cases to the highest judge operating within our capital city.
Agree to permit [rival] to handle these cases according to their laws.
Inform the [rival] emissary that we are pardoning these crimes.

events.text: A year has passed, and the emissary from [rival] returns, again demanding justice in the matter of several criminal cases. We have been able to gather more information, but not enough to clear any of our citizens of their charges. What will we do?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: No One Will Know

options.text: The lights dim.

events.text: It must have been poison. It had to be. You feel yourself, paralyzed, as you begin to slump. Across the table, [character] meets your eyes and holds them. "Goodbye" he mouths.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: No Surrender

options.text: We will defeat [rival], once and for all.
It is time to leave these troubles in the past.

events.text: The people of [rival] are crying out for war. The threat of [rival] has been a worry to your nation for too long and with the careless outbreak of a small local conflict in which a young boy was killed, war fervor has reached a new pitch. The families gather to give their blessing and to ask if you will rid the world of [rival], once and for all?

events.author: Solver
events.name: Old Opponent

options.text: I do not expect [character] to become a friend but I am willing to accept his service.
He may settle in [city] as a regular citizen if he swears an oath not to pursue politics.
[character] is no longer my equal. He is not coming back.

events.text: When you were just beginning your political career, [character] was a major politician in [city] and your main opponent. Son of a prominent strategos, [character] had both money and fame going for him but ultimately you proved to be the sharper politician and got [character] expelled through an ostracism vote. Years have passed and [character] may now return to [city]. You can ask him to serve in an official capacity, despite your past animosity, or perhaps it is better to let [character] live a quiet life.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Omens Turn True

options.text: All hail [character], new [title] of [rival].

events.text: This, then, is the moment from your dreams so long ago, when [character] was but an infant. Together, [character] and [character] have turned them all - the army, the court, the people of [rival]. It is unclear if leaving you with your life and freedom is a mark of mercy, or of contempt and spite.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: On the Payroll

options.text: Have your agents trail [character].
Take no chances and capture the traitor immediately.

events.text: [character] has caught wind of a traitor in your midst. The influence of the diabolical [character] has crept into your very court, his agents paying [character] vast amounts of money for information of your armies' movements. Should action be taken, [character] asks?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Out of the Ashes

options.text: Hold a grand triumph in [city], with a celebration lasting for weeks.
Send out diplomats with subtle warnings that [rival] is not to be crossed.

events.text: Your rivals, [rival], lay defeated, their people scattered to the winds and their cities in ruins. With this the once great nation is finally beneath the heel of your foot. History is yours to write.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Partnering with [character]

options.text: We will do great things together!

events.text: Another great Spartan warrior, [character], is ready to lead our people to victory. [character] is himself of royal blood and an experienced battlefield commander who has fought alongside your father-in-law. Now that [character] has returned from another of his expeditions, he is ready to stand shoulder to shoulder with you and face any threat the world may hold.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Passage of the Moon

options.text: Adopt this idea as the [character] Calendar.
How can we have an extra.25 days in a year!? Damn fool of a plan. Banish [character]!

events.text: [character] returns to court with a plan for a new calendar. He suggests implementing a system where each year contains 365.25 days. The passage of the moon demands it!

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Pax Romana

options.text: Commission inscriptions across the city, detailing your rule and how you have brought peace.
It is enough that the people are happy.

events.text: Across [rival] it is known that your rule has brought peace. There may still be some fighting, but compared to the era of civil wars and threats from rival empires this is a golden age. One historian has called it the Pax Romana, a phrase that is quickly catching on.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Perfect Crime

options.text: I am a master of intrigue.

events.text: Nobody seems to be any the wiser about your hand in the untimely death of your wife [character]...

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Personal Religion
events.text: Although [rival] has no state religion, many people follow their own faiths and practices. The [religion] of [city] say that the support of will only strengthen your rule and offer to teach you about their ways. Will you accept?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Pieface's Lessons

options.text: Pieface? He is simply a lovable prankster.
Tell the royal guards to refuse him.
Forty lashes for the fool!

events.text: On more than one occasion, the court fool, Pieface, has been discovered tutoring the royal children. His lessons? Tossing dung at the heads of the noble families, covering the palace walls with offensive scribble, and riding goats through the streets of [city]. Despite his pleasant demeanor, the buffoon may need to be banished.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Pilgrimage Concludes

options.text: I am glad everything turned out as it did.

events.text: The [rival] pilgrims in [city] are leaving the city after having visited the most important sites of [religion]. Some locals regarded the visitors with suspicion, but there was no trouble. On the contrary, many [rival] expressed hope that the war would soon be over, and one pilgrim family left a gift of [religion] scrolls for [city] as a token of gratitude for the peaceful reception.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Pining Chords

options.text: Support this new focus on the arts.
Demand that your heir starts acting the part.

requirements.label: Wanton / Debauched
tip: The leader must have one of: Wanton; Debauched

options.text: Organize some entertainment to distract [character].

events.text: Since [character] return to [rival], your heir [character] has taken to staying in his room, writing music to the love that was not to be. Your advisors are united in their suggestion that something must be done.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Plot Uncovered

options.text: Arrest everyone involved. Kill anyone who resists.
Let them know I will be merciful, though they did little to deserve that.

events.text: Your spies have uncovered a sinister conspiracy between [character] and the [family]. After your recent refusal to heed [character], he arranged for [family] help to murder you. It is not too surprising that [character] was working against you, but to go this far... after thanking your spies, it's time to decide how to deal with the plotters.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Plot by Heretics

options.text: I will not let them insult Aten, and I will not be told what to do.

events.text: Your husband [character] approaches you, holding a piece of parchment. He says you haven't been yourself ever since focusing on Aten, and that you're putting your own religious reforms ahead of your family and your people. [character] and his [family] allies have prepared a decree renouncing Atenism and restoring the priests' freedom to worship as they see fit. You only have to put your seal on the decree, something [character] demands in no uncertain terms.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Plots and Betrayals

options.text: Pursue them until they are apprehended.
Let them escape, but seize their belongings.

events.text: The treachery of [character] has been exposed. He was plotting your downfall. The courtier [character] appears to be involved as well! The two conspirators have fled the palace grounds. What shall we do?

options.text: n/a
n/a

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Poisoned!

options.text: Revenge will not save me.
Regicide is not acceptable.

events.text: Several weeks after the banquet with your heir, [character], you begin to experience strange visions. You suffer fainting spells and grow weak with fever. There is only one conclusion. When [character] offered you his cup, its contents were poisoned. The doctor predicts that you have less than one year to live.

events.author: Josh Unsworth

followsFrom.name: The One Who Would be King

events.name: Popular Support

options.text: Spread propaganda about our aim to defend the masses.
We must face these rebels on the field.

events.text: All attempts to stop the slave rebellion have failed. Furthermore, there have been mutterings of praise and admiration for the actions of the rebels amongst many of the lower classes. Many feel the yoke of our rule and their resentment lends strength to their resolve. The fire started by the initial revolt has spread and some of the people of [city] have even risen up to join forces with the rebellion. The court worries about the growing force, but encourage the use of this chance to appear sympathetic to the plight of the common people.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Prison Conscripts

options.text: Have [character] form a militia.
The army will deal with this.

events.text: A faction of the conscripts released from [city] have become disgruntled with the treatment that they have received in the army and have taken to raiding. [character] apologizes for the mistake and has asked to form a militia in the city to bring the prisoners to justice. How will you deal with this new threat?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Proof

options.text: This conflict will have to be resolved on the field of battle.

events.text: An emissary arrives from [rival] with a declaration of war. "We knew that you could not be trusted. Your threats delivered the final proof."

events.author: Dale
events.name: Pyramids of Pharaoh [character]

options.text: Allow [character] to hire guides and charge tourists.
Let the locals continue giving the tours.

events.text: [character] approaches you with a proposal. "Apologies for intruding on your grief, [character], but an opportunity has presented itself. Pyramids of Pharaoh [character] in [city] are attracting many travelers from far-away lands wishing to view the final resting place of Pharaoh [character]. Most of these travelers are asking locals to show them around Pyramids. I believe we could capitalize on this and hire some guides to run tours. We could sure use the Money gained from these..... let's call them, tourists."

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Quirinus

options.text: Take after his example and encourage an imperial cult.
Place statues of Quirinus across [rival].
Proclaim that your own successes are far beyond those of Romulus.

events.text: After the founder of Rome, Romulus, departed the world, a noble claims to have been visited by the deceased King while traveling. This noble claims that Romulus told him that he, Romulus, is actually the god Quirinus. It seems like a small step for one so powerful to be seen as divine. Will you encourage the worship of the founder of Rome?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Raising the Stakes

options.text: Agree to pay Tribute.
Call in the cavalry and prepare for War.

events.text: An emissary arrives from [rival]. "Our two nations stand on the brink of War. Your recent gift has opened an opportunity for you, however. Pay us more in tribute, and we will stay our armies." The court looks to you. Shall it be peace, or war?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Refusal to Die

options.text: I trust the [family] to handle this.
We must stop this threat quickly.

events.text: The gladiators of [city] have risen against you. Forced to fight for their lives day after day, the deadly warriors have been plotting and waiting for their chance. The reports read that a hundred or so escaped from the training school in [city], using kitchen utensils to kill the guards and fully arm themselves before making a break for the surrounding countryside. Many of the guards of [city] were killed in the fighting and the once-slaves are now armed and increasingly dangerous. Rumors of the escape spread around [rival] within the week. The news brings fear to the nobles, and hope to the dispossessed. The name on most lips is that of the rebel’s leader - a man named [character]. The [family] claim that there is nothing to fear and that they will handle the situation themselves. How shall we respond?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Religious Truce Ends

options.text: Very well, ready the armies.
Persuade the [rival] that there is no need to resume fighting.

events.text: The religious observances are complete and [rival] is ready. Their diplomats thank you for agreeing to the truce and announce that the war is to resume.

options.text: It is certainly afraid, but even an animal can overcome its fear with discipline.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Republic of Warriors

options.text: Accept their offer to bolster your forces.
Have them send any willing fighters to [city].
Ask them to train your [unit].

events.text: Your [unit] have been approached by a local warrior clan, a militaristic republic who live in the Jungle of [rival] and are fiercely protective of their land. Determined and loyal fighters, they are offering to join your forces to help defend their homes.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Resident Artist

options.text: Leave him to follow his own muse.
Place him in charge of royal beautification efforts.

events.text: After years of back-breaking labor and total devotion, [character] has finally completed his massive public painting, a true work of art. Visitors from neighboring cities have already begun to trickle into [city] to walk the promenade and view the magnificent mural. The court is proud of [character]'s accomplishments, and there is some discussion about whether he should be enlisted by the government.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Resistance to Atenism

options.text: Destroy temples to other gods. None shall be above Aten!
To protect the empire, we must allow worship of other gods. Aten will forgive this.
Explain to the priests that the gods they worship are but manifestations of Aten.

events.text: Facing the truth can be difficult, and the simple truth that Aten is the god of Egypt has been particularly difficult to accept for most of the priests and nobles. They're openly challenging the idea that there is just one god, and continue to worship in the old ways. Rumor has it, some of the priests say that even Hesat and Menhit are more important than Aten! There may not be an easy way out of the social upheaval we've caused.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Retribution

options.text: The memory of [character] will haunt me to the end...

events.text: You return to the palace and retire to your chambers to relax, it has been a long day but the decree has been announced that slavery will once again be a law in [rival]. Just as you start to rest, a strange commotion catches your ear. From the balcony you see fires across the palace and people running. Something is wrong. Seriously wrong. There is a clash in the corridor outside your rooms and you hear the grating of metal followed by sharp screams. A host of people march into your room, a mix of guards, servants and courtiers. “We were slaves once. Never again.” The cry is repeated as blade after blade buries itself in your body.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Returned to the Fold

options.text: Ratify the marriage before.
Denounce the bond between them.
[character] will return on his own.

events.text: [character] comes to you late one night and proposes a deal. As you helped him out before, he is willing to try and convince [character] to return from his elopement. Once [character] and his new husband [character] are back, [character] could ensure that their marriage is either accepted or condemned in the eyes of [religion].

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Returning Emissary

outcomes.label: Securing Peace Returning Emissary Misunderstanding War Main
Securing Peace Returning Emissary Misunderstanding War Fallback

options.text: ...accept our apologies and overlook the offense... for now.

events.text: The [tribe] emissary returns to court. He informs you that the [tribe] have decided to...

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Returning Emissary

options.text: The peace shall endure.

events.text: The [tribe] emissary returns to court. He thanks you for returning the prince and punishing your wayward subject, [character].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Returning to the Mysteries

options.text: The secrets gain clarity!

events.text: It is time for the annual ritual of the Cult Of The Mother in [city]. While you were previously an initiate, blindfolded and guided through the secrets by the experienced members, this time it is your turn to be the one showing the path to others. Seeing the new initiates go through what you did, their same confusion and desire to grasp the unknown, deepens your understanding of the Mysteries further than ever before.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Revealed Affair

options.text: It is still my child.

events.text: After several months, your condition becomes impossible to ignore. One night is all it took... Your husband agrees to look the other way as long as the child is born outside the royal line. Are you ready to welcome your new baby into the world?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Revelation on the Road

options.text: [character] is right, these persecutions must end.
Banish [character] from your court.

events.text: [character] comes before you a changed man. The zealous soldier tells of how he was overcome with a vision of the risen Christ, who called out his name and sent him forth to preach. Blinded by the incident, it was only in [city] that he was met by a [religion] teacher who healed his sight and baptized him. [character] is horrified by his previous actions persecuting the [religion], and asks that the religion be allowed to exist peacefully in [rival]. What reply will you give the new convert?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Revelation on the Road

options.text: Send [character] to organize the [religion] leaders.
Spend time asking [character] about his ideas about [religion].

events.text: [character] comes before you a changed man. The zealous soldier tells of how he was overcome with a vision of the risen Christ, who called out his name and sent him forth to preach. Blinded by the incident, it was only in [city] that he was met by a [religion] teacher who healed his sight and baptized him. [character] is horrified by his previous actions persecuting the [religion], and gives thanks that you prevented him from continuing the persecutions. He asks that the religion be allowed to exist peacefully in [rival]. What reply will you give the new convert?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Rightful Heir

options.text: Alas, I've found the throne rather comfortable.
Welcome back! The throne is yours, my King.

events.text: In the morning light, [character] sweeps into the court. Your courtiers gasp and gesture meaningfully among themselves. The distraught young leader who left the throne to his regent has matured into an imposing man. "I thank you for your fine efforts on my behalf," [character] says to you and the court. "But the time has come for me to retake my rightful inheritance - the throne you now sit upon." How shall you respond?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Rightful Heir

options.text: The throne is now yours, and yours alone.

events.text: [character] is dead before getting a chance to sit on the throne for which he was destined. With the rightful heir gone, the crown seamlessly transitions to yourself as the nobles and generals put their full support behind the one person with experience of leading [rival]. May you continue to lead us to glory!

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Riot in the Streets

options.text: Lock the traitors in shackles.
Buy their loyalty with gold.

requirements.label: Righteous / Blessed
tip: The leader must have one of: Righteous; Blessed

options.text: Try to reason with them.

events.text: Rebels loyal to the imprisoned usurper, [character], are rioting in the streets of [city]. They demand justice. We worry that this insurrection might spread. What shall we do?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Rise and Shine

options.text: Well, I guess I’m up now.
This dastardly creature will not keep me from my sleep!
Could this be… a sign from the gods?

events.text: You wake to the familiar dawn chorus of people moving through the palace, the smells of food being prepared in the kitchens below, and the soft but persistent weight resting on your feet... Weight on your feet!? Bolting upright, you come face-to-face with a chicken, nonchalantly sitting on the covers of your royal bed. It rests, watching you without any particular interest, with only the occasional cluck as if it were talking to itself. An experimental shake does nothing to shift the unexpected visitor who, if anything, seems to settle further into its new nest.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Rising Star

options.text: I shall consider carefully how to treat [character]...

events.text: [character] has become a rising star of [rival]! Rising Star is a powerful character with the ability to accomplish great things as a General, Governor, or a position on the Councilor. No nation ever has more than one Rising Star at a time. As Rising Stars accumulate experience points (Xp) in these positions, their power and reputation grow. Each new experience level they reach is a chance to rise even higher, with possibilities for intrigue or opportunity.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Ritual in the Dark

options.text: The secrets are revealed.

events.text: You descend into the darkness of the Mithraeum. There is silence in the dimly lit chamber as your fellow initiates watch you slowly approach the altar. The scene it depicts is now familiar to you: Mithras, the Unconquered Sun, slays a bull representing the moon, surrounded by a complex system of astrological symbols depicting the arrangement of the cosmos and the divine place of the god. The father draws his bow and aims at your heart. The bow creaks. Then silence. After ten heartbeats he lowers it again and the act is over, the wine is poured and the reverence broken. Just as Mithras ate over the body of the bull, as do you, the initiates relaxing into familiar conversation over the ritual feast.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Roma and her Malcontents

options.text: [character] will trouble me no longer.
Sorry, [character], but you've got to go.
Well, why not both?

events.text: With the rule of proscription, you have found an effective method of removing political enemies. Anyone you deem a threat to [rival] is added to the list, their lands immediately confiscated as property of the state, and a bounty placed on their head to be paid to anyone who kills them. The latest rounds could be a good chance to remove the ever troublesome [character]. However, you have also heard that [character] has some particularly wealthy estates that would surely be better looked after by yourself...

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Scholars In Arms - Research Complete

options.text: Splendid!

events.text: Research project complete!

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Second Expedition: Contact

options.text: It’s worth the price.
I think not!

events.text: A messenger has brought word from Sataspes, his contacts among the Saka gave him a cold greeting, still upset with the tactics he used to secure the previous deal. They will expand their trade with [rival] only if you pay premium prices. Sataspes asks that you send more funds as soon as possible.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Second Expedition: Contact

options.text: Excellent news!

events.text: A messenger has brought word from Sataspes, his contacts among the Saka welcomed him back fondly, and they are ready to expand their trade with [rival]. You need but await the arrival of their merchants.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Second Expedition: Results!

options.text: He served me well!

events.text: Another great merchant caravan has come to [city]. Sent by Sataspes, they have traveled huge distances to bring you their most precious goods. As before, a small but steady trade will continue to keep [city] supplied. Sataspes, it seems, has decided to journey to still more distant lands and is unlikely to be seen in [rival] again.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Second Expedition: Results!

options.text: Alas!

events.text: A bedraggled man, who claims he was a member of Sataspes’ expedition, has come before you to tell you of its fate. After failing to secure a second deal, the expedition was driven from the lands of the Saka in disgrace. At one point, bandits set upon them, and Sataspes was killed in the resulting fighting.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Secret Negotiations

options.text: I approve this trade mission.
This is not the time.

events.text: Ambassador [character] reveals to you that he has been working tirelessly with insiders on the [rival] court to secure a trade deal. Finally, he has an agreement that may prove beneficial. What shall we tell him?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Secret of the Fool

options.text: It is time to be rid of Pieface.
Long live Pieface!

events.text: Courts are always swimming with rumors. However, one recent bit of gossip strikes you as more unsettling than the usual whispers. Several of our minor courtiers claim that the boorish fool, Pieface, is in fact an heir to the throne of [rival]. Banished for his silly shenanigans, the young lunatic fled his homeland for a life of his own making. If you choose to believe the story...

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Shadow of War

options.text: We have been preparing. Time to call up the militia.
In addition to our research efforts, we have been training for this war.

events.text: A formal declaration of war has arrived from [rival]. The informant appears to have been correct.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Silver Jubilee

options.text: Prepare a royal spectacle for the people that they will not soon forget!
We shall thank the gods for their kindness, and pray for their continued blessing.
I shall take another husband! We shall enjoy song, wine, and companionship!

events.text: This year is a special year in the annals of the kings and queens of [rival]. [character] celebrates his Silver Jubilee, a reign of 25 years. How shall we prepare for the celebration to commemorate this joyous day?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Silver Jubilee

outcomes.label: New Ambition Two Max Level Unit

rewards.text: Progress ambition: Two Max Level Unit

outcomes.label: New Ambition Two Max Level Unit

rewards.text: Progress ambition: Two Max Level Unit

outcomes.label: New Ambition Two Max Level Unit

rewards.text: Progress ambition: Two Max Level Unit

options.text: I'm not feeling very ambitious right now.

events.text: This year is a special year in the annals of the kings and queens of [rival]. [character] celebrates his Silver Jubilee, a reign of 25 years. Shall we choose a new Ambition in celebration?

events.author: Solver
events.name: So Much Talk

options.text: So petty. So short-sighted.

events.text: Disagreements about the future of [rival] continue in the nation, and once again your background is questioned by some of the wealthier statesmen, who have themselves never as much as raised a sword. "There was Hamilcar," says one of them, "then there was Hasdrubal, now it is Hannibal. Warriors, all of them, not builders. So what if Hannibal has outlived his father and his brother. What future can he secure for us? One where we have no friends, no allies, and only our own army to rely on?" Nothing is to be gained for you by engaging in a public debate, but it is once again disappointing to see how much time some aristocrats spend on talking instead of working to improve [rival].

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Something Real

options.text: [character] does not compare to [character].
My marriage to [character] comes first.

events.text: [character] has returned, and you meet in an empty wing of the palace. Your attraction remains as strong as ever, but life has grown more complicated. Hoping to ease the pain of leaving, [character] asks for a declaration of your love. She will return but wishes to know your intentions before departing.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Spite Among Siblings

options.text: Guards, find [character] and kill him quietly.
[character] is not worthy of a quick death. Let him rot a few more years.

events.text: Your physicians recently informed you of your impending death, but there is still one grudge, one wrong that has not been set right - [character]. A part of you cannot bear the thought of [character] living longer than you. There is no doubt, he would gleefully dance on your grave.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Spousicide

options.text: A life for a life.
Jail for [character]!
Banish [character].
There’s no point losing another husband.

events.text: Terrible news greets you today, [character] has murdered [character] in a jealous rage! “Let’s see you favor a corpse!” he cries as your guards drag him away. You must decide what to do with him.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: State Religion

options.text: Teach me your ways.
Refuse their offer.

events.text: As the head of the [religion] nation of [rival], it is expected that you adhere to the tenets and practices of the faith, and be seen doing so. With religion being integrated so closely into daily social and cultural life, the remind you that a lack of faith only builds a distance between yourself and your subjects. They offer to teach you about their ways. Will you accept?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Stolen Statue

options.text: Send court spies to [city] to investigate.
This is a local concern.

events.text: The ancient statue we unearthed and later erected in [city] has been stolen. Local militias are baffled by the crime. What shall be done?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Stranger at the Door

options.text: Convince [character] to let [character] come home.
"Remove" [character] and replace him with [character].
Pressure the heir to stay in [rival] as a minister.

events.text: A stranger arrives on the steps of the palace. It takes a moment for you to recognize the scrawny, ragged figure as [character], the heir to the [rival] throne. In the years since your last encounter, he has changed considerably, maturing into an imposing young man. "You helped me once," he says. "Now I need your help again. I wish to return to [rival]."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Street Debate

options.text: We will reward him with luxuries and property.
He performed his service faithfully.
Our work to win over the [family] must continue.

events.text: Furious with our recent actions, [character] and a faction of his followers move to seize control of the court and overthrow the rule of law. But they never reach the forum. [character] and his own disciples intercept the mob outside in the streets, and a tense debate ensues. Thankfully, [character]'s skills and experience pay off, and he is able to prevent an explosive incident.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Stricter Rules

options.text: Angering the priests will anger the gods.
The [family] have gone too far.

events.text: The citizens of [city] have petitioned the court to revert the rules recently imposed by the [family] Clerics. They have grown in power and are increasing their demands for sacrifices and tribute from the other families. Do we wish to interfere?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Successful Assassination

options.text: At least their feuding is over.

events.text: [character]'s assassins have succeeded in their mission to kill your heir, [character], but your role in the plot has been discovered! Despite many taking similar payments to look the other way, the court is disgusted by your complicity in such murderous intrigues against your own heir.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Successful Assassination

options.text: I am relieved... but not proud.

events.text: [character]'s assassins have succeeded in their mission to kill your heir, [character]. The payment for your silence sits heavily. Luckily, no one knows that you were involved. It is best to forget...

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Sudden Return

options.text: Warmly welcome them back.
You are no longer welcome here, [character].

events.text: [character] strolls into court like he had never left. Loudly and publicly, he demands a welcome for himself and his new husband, [character].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Suspicious Sinking

options.text: A brisk swim to shore leaves you invigorated and none the worse for wear.

events.text: The first sign of danger is when [character] orders you to use a barge that he has specially prepared with one of his freedmen. As soon as you reach the deeper waters, the ship begins to collapse; a little too easily, you can't help but notice. It appears that your son has decided to start acting upon his suspicions.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Terror in [city]

options.text: Reinforce the guard to reassure the people.
Dispatch soldiers as bodyguards to the nobles until this is over.
I will give a speech in [city] to rally the people.
I can only hope this ends soon.

events.text: The two deaths at the cold baths of [city] are a subject of much talk in the city, but most people assumed - as did you - that it was an isolated event between the two nobles, a conflict or a lovers' spat. This changes now as two more people have been found dead, this time in the streets of [city]. Both had clearly struggled against their attacker, and one of the victims was found face down in a puddle. The city's nobles seem somewhat relieved that both these latest victims are just commoners, but the population at large is terrified. Someone is stalking the streets of [city] at night, looking for people to kill. As the city guard is questioning everyone who could have seen anything, it's clear that finding this killer is of paramount urgency.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Abomination of War

options.text: Offer peace, in return for a tribute.
Meet on even footing.
We will pay whatever is needed.
Such ideals cannot always last.

events.text: The war with [rival] is intolerable. To have such death and suffering on your hands is a stain on the conscience that cannot be undone. It may be too late, but perhaps there is a path to peace.

events.author: Solver
events.name: The Age of Zoroaster

options.text: My name shall be forever remembered as the greatest patron of [religion]!
Spiritual duty goes in hand with our earthly duty. We shall improve our material world to bring it closer to perfect unity with Ahura Mazda!
We must bring the [religion] faith to all the unbelievers!

events.text: The history of [rival] has entered a new era, an era of light, truth-seeking, and the path to righteousness, endeavors guided by [religion]. As this faith is now the official religion of [rival], what proclamation shall you make as the king of a [religion] nation?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: The Bastard's Body

options.text: Such a waste.

events.text: During the funeral preparations, you are taken aside by your investigators. They explain that the death was an accident: [character] had been seen drunkenly singing near the cliffs by multiple witnesses. Smashed jars of wine were also found near the body.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: The Bastard's Body

options.text: The law is clear.
I do not wish to prosecute this matter.

events.text: After the funeral for [character], your investigators inform you that [character] was intimately involved with the deceased. Furthermore, a young stable boy saw them arguing before [character] pushed [character] off the cliff. How shall we handle this damning evidence?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: The Bastard's Body

options.text: This shall be handled as required by law.
I do not wish to prosecute this matter.

events.text: Before the funeral for [character], your investigators return from the scene of the crime. "Your majesty, we questioned [character]. He witnessed [character] murder [character] and throw his body from the cliff to hide it. I believe him, my [title]. He has no reason to lie." What shall be done about [character]?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Blade Falls

options.text: Oh Nero.

events.text: Your death is short and unceremonial: One of [character] servants comes to your chambers with a sword. You know exactly what he is there for and cry out for him to strike your womb. The end is mercifully swift.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Book and the Sword

options.text: Send him forth to spread the word of God.
Convince [character] not to go.

events.text: [character] storms into your chambers, eyes filled with holy righteousness. The animated believer is frustrated at the number of worshipers of other religions apart from [religion], and seeks to redouble his efforts in spreading the word of God. His faith demands a journey to convert others to follow Christ. [character] has picked out [city] and [city] as his targets. Will you support this mission?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Captured Horse

options.text: The world will never know.

events.text: The news arrives on the last gasps of a wounded messenger: Disaster has struck. Armed bandits have interrupted the ritual, killing the guards and making off with the horse. That anyone would be so audacious as to actually threaten your rule is a shock. [character] seems wholly unsurprised by the news. However, the cunning villain seems content to watch you suffer in indignity without taking outright credit for the attack.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: The Child's Revenge

options.text: If.

events.text: A message has arrived from the [tribe], it seems they have a new war leader. One who is more than a little upset with us. "Years ago [rival] left me to die. But I didn't die, I found a new home with the [tribe] where I grew strong, and now I shall have my revenge upon you. If my armies take [city] they will raze it to the ground!"

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Coming [event]

options.text: We must hoard food supplies to prepare for the worst.
Earn favor with the citizens by hosting a feast, while we still can.
Make haste to secure alternate food sources.
Establish trade with our nearest neighbors.
[nation] shall prevail.

events.text: Each season sees the rain fall a little lighter on [rival]. The soil, once heavy and rich, now crumbles to dust in your hand. You know the land and have little doubt that a [event] will soon be upon us.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Companions

options.text: Yes, let us ride together!
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: The [unit] you lead are honored to ride by your side and take pride in being known as the elite cavalry of [rival]. It is not cheap to keep animals for riding, and many of the unit are nobles that you know from court. Used to protecting you and being in the thickest of the fighting has created a strong bond of loyalty and they have started referring to themselves as the Companions in honor of their place by your side. Shall we bestow this name officially as a sign of your favor?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Confessions

options.text: Spread the book as a warning against the sin of carnality.
You find yourself intrigued by the idea of a 'just war'.
Those early chapters sound much more fun!

events.text: [character] has spent much of the last year locked away, writing a unique style of text that blends together his personal history as a sinful youth with a contemplation on the nature of the soul. The text explores a wide range of theological ideas, inspired not only by his [religion] faith, but also his past as a follower of Neoplatonism and [religion]. The court is taken with these new ideas, but are keen to hear your judgment. Is there anything to learn in these writings?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Coup Succeeds

options.text: Abdicate. I concede and will go into exile.
Fight! I wish to die with a sword in my hand.

events.text: In a shocking turn of events, your brother, [character], has succeeded in the plot against you. He enters court with [character] and his other supporters, ready to take the throne. What is your last command?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Coup Succeeds

options.text: Abdicate. I concede and will go into exile.
Fight! I wish to die with a sword in my hand.

events.text: In a shocking turn of events, your brother, [character], has succeeded in the plot against you. He enters court with [character] and his other supporters, ready to take the throne. What is your last command?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Cult of Mithras

options.text: Accept the cult of Mithras.
Curtail the spread of this god.

events.text: The Cult Of Mithras has started to spread through the army, brought by new [family] recruits from [city]. The worshipers gather in small groups and build sunken shrines where they meet in darkness. That is as much as is publicly known; the acts of the cult are a secret, revealed only to those who are initiated into the Mysteries. [character] asks you to join the Cult Of Mithras, assuring that despite the [rival] trappings of this new god, he bears no relation to the counterpart in their pantheon. Will you accept?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Death of Reason

options.text: [character] will be always be remembered as a martyr.
Have [character] arrested for this, these horrors are unforgivable.
[religion] will no longer be supported by the crown.

events.text: The situation in [city] has continued to deteriorate, with the religious turmoil and rioting deepening divides between the city’s communities. Many are desperate for the fighting to end, so when rumors start spreading that the pagan [character] is influencing [character] and turning him against making peace, they see their chance. The mob gathers outside of [character] house to intimidate her, but when she is found in the street a frenzy breaks out. [character] is pulled from her chariot, stripped and lynched with roof tiles, her body burned outside of the city walls. It is unclear how much the mob was influenced by [character], but hefty bribes have been paid to avoid repercussions in court.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Defector

options.text: Yes, we should recruit him while we can.
This is not the time.

events.text: Chancellor [character] has learned that a high-ranking member of the [rival] court wishes to flee his homeland. However, he requires an escort to secure his escape from the country and find refuge in [rival]. Do we risk our relationship with [character] to assist this defector?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: The Dye is Cast

options.text: [character] shall serve in the court.
[character] shall direct our scientists.

events.text: Scientific analysis has shown the hair dye to be harmless indeed. On further investigation many of the female customers have shamefacedly admitted that they reverted to use of the lead and sulphur concoction soon after purchase because their husbands and lovers preferred its colour range. How shall we handle this matter?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Empress of [city]

options.text: This experiment has gone far enough.

events.text: The city of [city] has been thriving during its autonomous rule, the leadership of [character] taking the city from strength to strength. A recent economic boom has seen the city minting new coins, with inscriptions that name [character] an empress, and so an equal to yourself. Is such hubris to be tolerated?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The End of Autonomy

options.text: We will take back [city], by any means.
No, the city has earned its freedom.

events.text: The city of [city] has become renown as a free state of autonomous rule, a land unto itself. The court begrudges the situation, complaining that allowing such freedoms encourages others to expect the same. The situation reaches a head when [character] stands before the court and demands that something be done. [city] will not return to the fold without the use of force. Shall we fight to regain control?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The End of Peace

options.text: We return to the art of war.

events.text: A fleeting dream, the time of peace is at an end.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Envoy Returns

options.text: Very impressive, [character].
That's all well and good, but did you learn anything useful about [character]?

events.text: [character] has returned safely, boasting of his visit to the [tribe]. While there, he claims to have debated a [tribe] trader on the strengths of their different ways of life, extolling the virtues of [rival] civilization. The court clamor to hear the tales of his travels. [character] acts as if he has survived a stroll through a lion’s den. Perhaps he did.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Face of Gold

options.text: I will be depicted as incarnate.
We will depict the old gods, symbols of our nation's pride.
The symbols of [religion] will grace our coins.
No gods will grace our coins, only mortals.

events.text: With the ongoing Monetary Reform, [character] and [character] have both raised the question of what images are to be used on the newly printed coins. Each believes that the symbols of their religion has the best claim to be stamped onto the new coins. What imagery will be used on the reformed coins?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Final Days of Mani

options.text: The Prophet is dead.

events.text: News has reached your court of the final days of [character]. Caught and imprisoned for 26 days in [rival] cell, the prophet was guarded day and night, only tended to by three faithful followers. [character] foresaw his imminent death and embraced it, preparing his immortal soul for its final journey to the realm of light. It was not long before he closed his eyes for the last time. Furious that his prisoner escaped execution, [character] has had the head cut off the body and displayed above the gates of [city].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Final Days of Mani

options.text: The Prophet is dead.

events.text: News has reached your court of the final days of [character]. Caught and imprisoned for 26 days in [rival] cell, the prophet was guarded day and night, only tended to by three faithful followers. [character] foresaw his imminent death and embraced it, preparing his immortal soul for its final journey to the realm of light. It was not long before he closed his eyes for the last time. Furious that his prisoner escaped execution, [character] has had the head cut off the body and displayed above the gates of [city].

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Final Message

options.text: This is my last breath...

events.text: Memories of the mysterious writing continue to haunt you, even as ruling occupies your mind with other matters. Unfortunately, anxiety over the ghostly message takes its toll. After weeks of ill health, weakening resolve, and useless cures, you feel the breath of life slip from you. Perhaps the writing on the wall was an omen after all.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Forewarned Hour

options.text: Let us hope our preparations are enough.

events.text: Just as [rival] warned, the horizon around [city] is darkened by the banners of the oncoming horde. The enemy is at the gates.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Forgotten Prophet

options.text: Agree to search for the cave together.
It is not worth starting trouble with [rival].

events.text: our messenger weaves his way to the palace in [city], presenting your findings before the court. The audience is not a success, the [rival] treating the messenger with hostility before the [title] tersely tells him to leave. However, the messenger is approached by another when leaving the city, a discontent minister who tells the whole story: [character] ancestor was the prophet, but after the nation's adoption of [religion] their royal family have made every effort to destroy all records of their ancestor's [religion] faith. The courtier offers to reveal the location of a cave where the prophet resided, if you allow him to join the court of [rival].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Forgotten Prophet

options.text: Agree to her price.
Refuse, and be content with your findings.

events.text: It is almost a full year before you find someone who is able to decipher the obscure writing and provide an explanation for the story, an explorer who spends her days searching through ruins for artifacts and lost relics. The findings are worth the wait. After translating the text, she reveals that [title] [character] ancestor was also the prophet. It appears that after [rival] adoption of [religion] their royal family have made every effort to destroy all records of their ancestor's [religion] faith. The explorer asks one thing in return for the information. She has the location for a cave where the prophet resided, but will share it for a promise of the first choice of any relics that are found.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Fourth Philosophy

options.text: Rein [character] in, to try an avoid escalating the tensions.
Crack down on the zealots, enforcing military law in the city.
Convince the Fourth Philosophy that you believe in their cause.

events.text: In his writings about the history of [religion], [character] has been particularly antagonistic to a group of [religion] believers in [city] whom he calls the Fourth Philosophy. The writer blames them for many of the troubles in the city, claiming that they are little more than robbers and bandits. The feeling is mutual, with their retorts being that he is but a traitor to the religion, too weak to follow through with his beliefs. The sect are unafraid to fight for their zealous beliefs.

events.author: Benjamin Gautron
events.name: The Golden Spearmen

options.text: Let them shine in our name!
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: The [unit] you lead guard your side at all hours and monitor all other units assigned as bodyguards. Their absolute loyalty is of course paramount to their role and as a sign of honor they are equipped with the most resplendent of our arms and armors. People have taken to calling them "The Golden Spearmen". Shall we recognize this name as an additional honor?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Harii

options.text: All shall fear the Harii!
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: [character] has been leading the [unit] with a steady hand. Many of the unit are now Germanic tribesmen drawn to his banner. [character] has been leading the troops in unusual tactics, painting themselves in black tar and attacking at night to strike fear into the enemy. The army talks about these warriors in a uncertain mixture of awe and fear. [character] asks that we grant his unit the name Harii so that the enemy know who to fear.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: The Heir's Cup: Payoff

options.text: It's good to be [title]!

events.text: You celebrate the payoff of your master plan. By poisoning your way to the throne you've come into power so much sooner than you otherwise would have!

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Hidden Child

options.text: I would do it again.
Sometimes, one makes the wrong decision.

events.text: In a private moment, you are approached by [character], a longtime advisor. "I wish to warn you," he says. "You know me as [character], but that is not my true name. I was born many years ago to an imprisoned mother. While you refused to grant her freedom, you stole me away to live a life of desperate solitude." He regards you with a steely gaze. "Retribution is coming."

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Holy Places

options.text: Go, with my blessing.
No, there is no time for such a journey.

events.text: [character] has requested to go on a pilgrimage to the [religion] Holy City of [city] to pay respect to and to. Will you grant permission for [character] to leave on this holy journey?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Ides of March

options.text: Et tu?

events.text: Beware the Ides of March!

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Immortals

options.text: The Immortals will always stand to protect [rival].
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: The [unit] led by [character] have proved themselves loyal and fierce fighters, elite warriors who bring fear to their enemies. Every time a member of the unit falls ill or is wounded, another is brought to fill the space. [character] asks that you recognize the unit and grant them the honor of being named the Immortals, to serve your dynasty for all time.

events.author: Solver
events.name: The Impostor

options.text: Does the truth matter? He will never forgive me and so he cannot be allowed to live.
He is indeed an impostor. Agreeing to serve me is Gaumata's only chance at power.
[character] is the rightful king, and I made a terrible mistake. I must admit the plot and restore him to power.

events.text: You took the throne by deposing [character], who ruled for mere weeks. [character] would have been the legitimate king... except that this man is not [character]. His real name is Gaumata and he had somehow found out that the real [character] had been murdered, so Gaumata shamelessly impersonated the king, at least until you uncovered his lie. That is the story you have told, in any event. What is the truth, wise king? Who is this man really and what shall be done about him?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Karpans

options.text: Take action to curb the spread of [religion].
Tell the Karpans and [family] to stop their persecutions.

events.text: There has been resistance to the spread of [religion] in [rival]. Some of the priestly caste of [religion], called the Karpans, are vehemently against the reforms of the new religion and have managed to persuade the [family] to support their cause.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Long Life of the Dead

options.text: I've always done what is best for [rival].
I can’t go on like this, not one more day.

events.text: You wake to a night that is dark and deathly quiet but for the pounding of your heart. For many years you have found satisfaction in ruling [rival], but lately your thoughts fall on the dark past. Were you justified in your role in removing [character] from the throne, all those years ago, or was it a young man’s ambition gone too far?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Lost Scrolls

options.text: Study them yourself.
Give them to your scholars.
Return them to the [religion] priests.

events.text: [character] comes to you with news of an amazing discovery. A series of caves has been found by the coast near [city], containing [religion] scrolls from generations ago. It seems that whoever left them there gave their lives to protect the scrolls. [character] asks what you want done with the discovered scrolls.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Medjay

options.text: Grant them this honor.
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: The [unit] have shown themselves to be strong and capable warriors, an example that the other troops of your armies look up to. [character] suggests that he could train them into an elite force of defenders for protecting our cities. Should they be given this honor of being named the Medjay?

events.author: Solver
events.name: The Menace Eliminated

options.text: These sad events show the importance of a good city guard.
Perhaps mass celebrations in [city] would help its citizens make new good memories.
The killer's execution should be public. And, of course, slow...

events.text: [city] is now safe from the killer that stalked the city! The city guard did not rest for a moment after his second attack, and their hard work has paid off. The guards tracked down the killer and found him living in an abandoned leathercrafter's workshop. It did not take much coaxing for the killer to confess to the recent murders, and to planning more of them in [city]. He even said that the most satisfying kill of all would have been to kill you, [character]. It will take a long time for [city] to forget these difficult times.

events.author: Solver
events.name: The Menace Eliminated

options.text: These sad events show the importance of a good city guard.
Perhaps mass celebrations in [city] would help its citizens make new good memories.
The killer's execution should be public. And, of course, slow...

events.text: [city] is now safe from the killer that stalked the city! The city guard did not rest for a moment after his second attack, and their hard work has paid off. The guards tracked down the killer and found him living in an abandoned leathercrafter's workshop. It did not take much coaxing for the killer to confess to the recent murders, and to planning more of them in [city]. He even said that the most satisfying kill of all would have been to kill you, [character]. It will take a long time for [city] to forget these difficult times.

events.author: Benjamin Gautron
events.name: The Mesedi

options.text: And their leader should be honored too!
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: The [unit] led by [character] have proven their military skill and above all, their unconditional loyalty to your person. You have taken to relying on them as bodyguards and leading them is a great honor, which [character] clearly enjoys. He suggests that their excellence might be further encouraged if you gave them the honor of an official name.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Missing Envoy

options.text: This will not go unanswered.
We will take [character] word, for now.

events.text: The party that accompanied [character] to the [tribe] has returned to [city], without [character]. They claim that [character] disappeared on the fourth night and was not seen again. [character] claimed to have no knowledge of the disappearance, and told them to return home.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Numerus Batavorum

options.text: My guards will be loyal only to my dynasty.
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: Originally bought for money, the mercenary [unit] have proved themselves loyal and staunch fighters. A thought occurs to you that it could be useful to have a unit of bodyguards that are not loyal to the noble families and have no interest in the politics of court. Shall we name this unit and rise them in honor?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Path to Freedom

options.text: Allow [character] to proceed with his plan.
It is not worth the risk. We will stand and fight.

events.text: [character]’s force now threatens the very heart of [rival]. The court is in complete disarray at the idea of the vengeance of those that they once enslaved. Chaos takes hold as the blame for the dire situation is thrown around the court. The motives of the rebels are not yet known. Are they aiming to attack the capital? To escape your lands? To end slavery completely? [character] offers a last gambit - to send a message offering ships to those in the rebel camp. If even a few were to take the offer, it would divide their forces enough for a raid. Success would put an end to the threat without violence, but failure would likely see the army's support grow to such a size that they would take the initiative to attack.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Persecutor [character]

options.text: Invite the commander to serve you as a soldier.
Ask [character] to oversee the organization of such purges across the nation.
Protect the [religion] and demand that he desists at once.

events.text: There are tales of a commander in [city], relentless in his persecutions of the [religion] population. Filled with an uncommon zeal, [character] doggedly pursues the faithful in his attempts to destroy the church of Christ. Should this soldier be allowed to continue in his ruthless ways?

events.author: Solver
events.name: The Plight of Masabates

options.text: I will not stand for this! Let [character] try her insidious schemes, but Masabates walks free.
It is a despicable act, but I am not prepared to openly challenge [character].

events.text: Your mother in law [character] continues to show herself a most despicable and cruel person. This time her chosen victim is Masabates, one of [character]'s servants. [character] offered [character] a game of dice for Masabates, and your husband foolishly agreed - and lost. Now Masabates is about to be cruelly executed in [city] as [character] mocks [character] as powerless. As influential as [character] is, you are the queen and the people support you. Will you allow this execution to commence?

options.text: <p.is_sub.S1=SUBJECT_ZEALOT>The gods shall protect me!<p=SUBJECT_SCHOLAR>I shall research counters to common schemes.<p=SUBJECT_ORATOR>Perhaps I can talk him out of it?<p=SUBJECT_DIPLOMAT>Perhaps I can talk him out of it?<p=SUBJECT_SCHEMER>He cannot out-plot me!<p=SUBJECT_HERO>He dares plot against me?!<p=SUBJECT_TACTICIAN>He can be easily out-maneuvered.<p=SUBJECT_COMMANDER>He is no threat to me!<p=SUBJECT_BUILDER>I hate these distractions from my great works.<p=SUBJECT_JUDGE>But… that’s illegal!<else>Worrisome.<end>

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Pox Spreads

options.text: We must continue to fight with science.
Prayers and rituals are the only remedy.
This disease will run its course.

events.text: The deadly pox continues to ravage [city], laying low much of its population. Even worse, individuals in [city] have begun showing symptoms. Both [character] and [character] have taken to their beds. Not even the court is safe...

events.author: Dale
events.name: The Priests of Amun

options.text: Order the guards to remove the Priests and throw them in prison.
Kneel before the Priests and beg forgiveness by denouncing Atenism.

events.text: You are leading worship at the Altar Aten in [city] when several Priests of Amun push through the crowd. As the group reaches the foot of the steps leading to the raised Altar, their leader raises his staff. Taking each step slowly he bellows in a thunderous voice, "Pharaoh! We condemn your soul to wander the sands of the Great White Desert for all of eternity! We ban you from the afterlife in Sekhet A'Aru where your forefathers linger! We curse any who meet your ghostly soul in the Great White Desert to an eternity wandering next to you!"

events.author: Josh Unsworth

followsFrom.name: The One Who Would be King

events.name: The Raid on [city]

options.text: We will send all the aid we can.
We must face these rebels on the field.

events.text: All attempts to stop the slave rebellion have failed. Emboldened by their victories, the rebels make a strike on [city], capturing resources and encouraging many of the slaves there to also rise against their masters. The court worries about the growing force, but the [family] Family demands that the focus should be on aiding the city.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Rebel Writer

options.text: We need a strong military advisor.
Write a history of [religion].
I have no need for you.

events.text: One of your courtiers reminds you of a rebel general and writer who once predicted your rise to leadership. Exactly as he claimed the [religion] God told him, [character] is dead and you are on the throne. The man is brought before you. He looks pleased to see you on the throne and promises to serve faithfully if you will set him free. He has spent the intervening years researching and amassing sources in order to write a history of [religion], or he could lead your troops into battle. What is his fate?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Return Home

options.text: I welcome his words. Let's try the dates.
I am known to like my wines.

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: Burn incense and let's put this behind us.

events.text: [character] returns home with flowery words and grateful gestures. He has brought back gifts of dates, spiced wines, and incense. He insists on acceptance of his gifts, as a sign of your forgiveness.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Return Home: The Dates

options.text: I should have never trusted [character]!

events.text: You are gripped by stomach aches and high fever. Sweats and nausea. "I think those dates will be the end of me."

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Return Home: The Incense

options.text: I should have never trusted [character]!

events.text: The incense follows you from room to room. You cry out, "What are those voices I hear, like ghosts from my past. They will not leave me alone!"

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Return Home: The Wine

options.text: I should have never trusted [character]!

events.text: You suddenly feel very weak. Summon the doctors - perhaps there was poison in that wine!

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Rise of Pieface

options.text: Send a fool to entertain his court.
Marvel at the gods' sense of humor.

events.text: Under the cloak of darkness, Pieface the fool flees the palace, escorted by a group of loyal [rival] followers. Their plot has come to fruition. The rulers of [rival] were murdered at their own banquet table, leaving the path open for Pieface. Now Pieface, the true heir, will be elevated to the throne, as ruler of all [rival].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Rise of Sulla

options.text: I am the ruler, not this young upstart.

events.text: A promising young officer and politician, [character], has been gaining fast prominence amongst the aristocratic elite of [rival]. The aging senatorial families still take offense at your rise from an equestrian family to a position of power, despite your years of rule. They are clearly backing [character] as a contender for the leadership of [rival].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Road to Glory

options.text: [rival] goes boldly into a new age of prosperity!

events.text: It is done. People from Kings to farmers know you as 'the Great', the exemplar of kingly values. All hail!

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Road to Glory

options.text: The wheels keep on turning.

events.text: The wheels of fate are not kind to all, especially those who reach for greatness. [character] ambition dies with him. May the rulers to come have better fortunes!

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Sacred Band

options.text: Let their name bring fear to our enemies.
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: The [unit] serving under [character] come from all walks of life and social classes. There are only two prerequisites for serving in his unit. The first is the ability to fight, and fight well. The second is more unusual, the unit consists only of pairs of lovers. [character] says that the practice keeps the unit strong as a warrior would rather protect their lover than flee the field. Others in the army have taken to calling this unusual unit the Sacred Band. Shall we make the title official?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Sacred City

options.text: We shall thank for this victory.

events.text: [city] is ours! The Holy City of [religion] is now a part of [rival], providing a new lease of control over the dealings of the Religion. [rival] is filled with songs and chants, praising priests for delivering the city into your hands, so clearly led by the divine.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Sacred and the Profane

options.text: The world of The Sacred and The Profane awaits.

events.text: The gods of [rival] watch closely. Religion is not yet a question of faith but an act of everyday life, collections of rituals and rites developing in an attempt to avoid the calamitous ruin of a god’s anger. But this is a time of change, when not even divinity is constant. New gods and heroes attract followers to their social and mystical Local Cult, while world religions emerge and spread, seeking to establish their legal and theological footing amongst the common people and the courts of royalty alike. New leaders, the Clergy, guide the faithful, whose reverent passion can spill into the streets as Religious Dissent if not appeased. Tread carefully as you navigate these rituals and religions; the beliefs of a nation may see it rise or fall.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Search for Ostanes

options.text: Welcome [character].

events.text: The people you send to search for Ostanes spend a year following leads across [rival], aided by a local guide [character]. At different points they suspect an illegitimate child of [character], an advisor in his court or a long-dead descendant of Zoroaster. They finally come to the conclusion that the mage is simply a myth. Although there is no sign of Ostanes, [character] asks to join your court as a talented scholar in her own right.

events.author: Josh Unsworth

followsFrom.name: The One Who Would be King

events.name: The Slave General

options.text: [city] must be well protected!
We must face these rebels on the field.

events.text: All attempts to stop the slave rebellion have failed. Emboldened by the rebellion of the slaves under [character], the slaves of [city] have also thrown down their masters. Although the court hoped that the two factions would fight each other, the general leading the troops from [city] has sworn fealty to [character], bolstering the rebel forces even further. The court worries about the growing force, but the [family] demand that the we focus on increasing our training and raising a new force to protect [city].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Spy

options.text: Allow [character] to proceed with his plan.
It is not worth the risk. We will stand and fight.

events.text: [character]’s force now threatens the very heart of [rival]. The court is in complete disarray at the idea of the vengeance that those they once enslaved may inflict. Chaos takes hold as the blame for the dire situation is thrown around the court. [character] comes before you and offers a last gambit - to try and pay off a spy to let his forces into the rebel camp. Success would put an end to the threat without violence, but failure would likely see the army's support grow to such a size that they would take the initiative to attack.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Statue Complete

options.text: This wonder shall be known across the world.

events.text: The temple is complete. Stepping into the hallowed hall, the statue of looms above all, the light from the oil lamps catching details on the gold and ivory and giving the illusion of life. The sheer scale and craftsmanship is an awesome sight to behold. Tales of the Statue of are soon spreading across [rival] and beyond.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Travels of Mani
