options.text: Send him out to learn more of the spiritual and physical worlds.
No, his wisdom is needed here.

events.text: [character] has come before you with a request to go traveling across the world. The Manichaeism prophet first went east many years ago and there found divine inspiration. [character] is hoping that this journey will bring similar discoveries and bring him ever close to divine revelation. Will you let the prophet go on his travels?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Treasures of [city]

options.text: Sell it all.
Lavish our capital, [city], in refinements.
Use the hoard to help restore the city.

events.text: Following the taking of [city], you discover a large quantity of hidden art, temple refinements, luxury textiles, and more.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The True God Aten

options.text: Aten is the one god of [rival].
Aten is the one god, and his cult will spread across [rival].
No, we cannot abandon the old gods.

events.text: Under your divine rule [rival] has grown close Aten, the temples filled with the sound of harps and hymns praising the sun disk and your divine name. Not all are happy with the changes. [character] is especially upset, worried about the lessening power of the priests and the claims that only you can hear the words of Aten. But are you not the one divine intermediary as the divine ruler, child of Aten and the one visited in dreams? And your dreams of late have shown that Aten is the one true god, beyond creation and the giver of all life. Will you name Aten as the one true god?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Wandering Horse

options.text: Thank the guards for their service.
Spread the message as a sign of your legitimacy.
Surely I am blessed!

events.text: After a year spent roaming around [rival] lands, the horse has remained free. With great ceremony, it is led back to the palace and sacrificed. There is much celebration at this sure sign of the validity of your rule.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Weak Link

options.text: Send [character] to remove [character] once and for all.
Decide against it. You are stronger together.

events.text: While you share rule with [character], your power grows each day as his wanes. With your son already named as heir, is there a reason to keep [character] around? Perhaps it is time to speed nature along.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Ziggurat Crumbles

options.text: I fail to see much benefit in such a building, but the people seem to like it.
We cannot afford it. Besides, it is an old building whose purpose has long been forgotten.
Not only shall we restore this important relic of our nation's history. We will improve it!
Perhaps while restoring it we can learn why our ancestors built it and how.
Let’s add to its grandeur by building an inner shrine dedicated to [religion].

events.text: The building techniques of our forebears were sadly lacking. Great Ziggurat has suffered over time and is barely recognisable. If the decay continues, it may soon be lost forever.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The [religion] of [city]

options.text: Welcome the back to your court.
Encourage [character] to stay in [rival] to grow the [religion] community.

events.text: [character] sends a message from [city]. Despite initial hostility and skepticism, a small but flourishing [religion] community has grown in the city. Having trained some religious leaders to oversee the new followers, [character] is ready to return to court.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The execution of [character]

options.text: [city] will burn for this.
We can only hope that one day [city] will be as welcoming of other faiths as us.
Stir up fervor against [rival].
He will be remembered.

events.text: A message of dark tidings has arrived from [city]. Despite initial success, [character] was met with hostility and skepticism. Perhaps too fervent in his attempts at conversion, tensions reached a breaking point and [character] was captured and executed by the city officials for disturbing the peace.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Their Deathless Gaze

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Agree with [character] statement.
Attempt to lighten [character] spirits by declaiming [character] idea.

events.text: The evening passes by in amiable conversation before the topic of the [family] dinner turns to the nature of law. [character] gives a long and impassioned speech on how the gods are the judges of us all and so the ultimate source of law. “But then we are all lost causes!" [character] quips, "The gods judge that it is evil to die, or else they would do so themselves.” [character] opens his mouth to retort, before rethinking and retreating to stare contemplatively into his wine, silent in the way that only those whose world-view has just been irrevocably shaken are.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: They Always Make a Mistake

options.text: [character] deserves the execution of a common criminal.
He will rot in the dungeons.

events.text: It is perhaps a week before the captain of the guard disturbs you at a late hour, along with an entourage of subordinates and the bound and bloodied form of [character] carried between them. "My [title], we found him lurking in a hay bale just outside the palace grounds. What are your orders?"

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Those They Spared

options.text: Allow [character] to proceed with his plan.
It is not worth the risk. We will stand and fight.

events.text: [character]’s force now threatens the very heart of [rival]. The rebels have adopted a new strategy of letting any who surrender live if they lay down their arms and flee. The offer of clemency both weakens the resolve of our warriors and means that the rebels can collect the weapons and armor, becoming increasingly well equipped. While the rest of the court falls to chaos and despair, [character] offers a last gambit - to use this tactic against the slaves, waiting until they are collecting weapons and then attacking with a hidden force. Success would put an end to the threat without violence, but failure would likely see the army's support grow to such a size that they would take the initiative to attack.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Three Weeks

options.text: Of course, the marriage will be forgotten.
You must live with your consequences, the marriage will stand.
You are no longer welcome here, [character].

events.text: [character] returns from his elopement in regret and shame. It turns out that the romance only lasted for three weeks before the two could no longer stand each other and went separate ways. Hanging his head, [character] asks that you annul the marriage. Will you accept him back?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Time Moves On

options.text: Align yourself with [character] detractors.
Stay carefully silent.

events.text: Reputations are fickle things. [character] has held his for a long time, but the cracks are showing. Few these days turn to him for inspiration or answers. When he is spoken of at all, it is only new and probing questions about his true deeds and motives.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tit for Tat

options.text: Surely, this is an empty threat.

events.text: Much time passes before at last you hear a response from [character] and [character] on the matter of your knowledge, and their cooperation. "One who wishes to make a threat should consider carefully their own vulnerabilities. Try and break apart that which we find dear, and see how long before tragedy strikes your own beloved."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tit for Tat

options.text: Excellent.

events.text: A delicate balance has been achieved, [character] and [character] continue their dalliance untroubled. In exchange, the houses [family] and [family] have been uncharacteristically united in support of your rule.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: To Be A King

options.text: I will remain king, no matter what it takes.
I will not entertain such thoughts!

events.text: When you were regent you were the ruler in every meaningful way, but being [title] still feels different. The decisions, the worries, the power, the benefits are all yours. There is so much to be accomplished and there are still rumors that [character] will one day return to the throne. An unbidden thought stirs, that perhaps [rival] would be better off if the Rightful Heir was to depart this world...

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: To Be A King

options.text: I am the one true [title]!

events.text: With the death of [character], your position as [title] is secure. The people praise your name in the streets and ask the gods to favor you and your reign. [rival] is in your hands, [character].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: To Be A King

options.text: It was not meant to be...

events.text: The fall of [character] is complete when documents are found after his death, detailing a desire to see [character] dead. The rumors of division and treachery in the royal family spread around the court, tarnishing the unntouchable throne.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: To Be A King

options.text: It was not meant to be...

events.text: The fall of [character] is complete when documents are found soon after your coronation, detailing a desire to see you, [character], dead. Hearing of the discovery, [character] flees into the night to escape justice. The rumors of division and treachery in the royal family spread around the court, tarnishing the unntouchable throne.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tough Negotiation

options.text: And that is how you negotiate! I accept.
If these people are so important, they will do well in [city].

events.text: Your intuition was right. Even though the [rival] pilgrims headed to [city] did not look like much, some important people turned out to be among them, including and. After what our envoys describe as a tough and unpleasant negotiation, [rival] is willing to pay us tribute and cease the fighting in exchange for safe return of the hostages.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Trial of the Scipios

options.text: Despite your innocence, offer to make a donation to the people
Declare that you mean to lead Rome until your last breath.
Is leadership worth such constant struggle? Maybe it is time to retire...

events.text: Rome shall never again fall under the thumb of a tyrant. This one determination dictates many of Rome’s laws and political life. The [family] have grown wary of your continued successes and popularity with the people. In a show trial, [character] claims that you have built your support with bribes taken from enemies of Rome and have even stolen from the national treasuries. Giving no pause for doubt, you tear down the accusations in a dramatic speech, listing your actions to defend Rome and tearing up your accounts in front of the watching politicians. To drive the point home that you will not be moved, you lead the adoring public in an impromptu procession to the gods of Rome. It is with grim satisfaction that you observe the embarrassment of your accusers. Yet is power worth this infernal politicking?

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tribal Conversion

options.text: We have been richly rewarded for converting the [tribe]!

events.text: Another messenger arrives bearing news from the recent [religion] High Synod: "We are greatly pleased that you have brought the formerly pagan [tribe] into the fold of [religion]. The light of the divine grows ever greater!"

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Tribe Slayer

tip: As leader: +50 Unit Trait XP / Infantry
As governor: +100 Unit Trait XP / Infantry

options.text: Admonish [character] for his recklessness.
Celebrate the victories in the capital!
Stay silent.

events.text: Acting independently of the military command, [character] and a squad of loyal soldiers and mercenaries raid the camps of the [tribe]. The battle is pitched and bloody. It calls to mind [character]'s skirmishes along the border during his years in training. Triumphant, the war party emerges with a victory over the [tribe]... and the head of [character].

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Troubled Companion

options.text: No. I cannot support this.
Yes. You have my blessing.
Perhaps we can discuss this in a dark alley later.

events.text: Your favored companion, [character], recently elevated to general, seems troubled of late. Drunken escapades do little to lift his mood until one evening he professes to be in love with [character]. He wishes to marry him and asks for your blessing, despite the obvious issue that [character] does not love him, but rather you. Or so you hope. Whom do you love more, [character] or [character], and how will you respond to [character]'s request?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: True Inheritance

options.text: We will tell the people of [rival] the truth.
We must choose a new heir secretly.

events.text: Late one morning, servants discover the heir, [character], missing from his chambers. According to a farewell message, he has departed [city] to meet his lover, [character], the heir to [rival]. There is nothing to be done.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Turning the Tables

options.text: I know [character] considered killing me. He was wrong not to. I will not make the same mistake.
Brilliant schemer or not, he has shown himself a coward. [character] will fear me and will serve me well.

events.text: You have returned to the throne as the rightful ruler of [rival], despite the attempts of [character] to declare you an impostor. On the one hand, what [character] did is unforgivable. On the other hand, his brief attempt to rule seems to have terrified him, and [character] is certainly a masterful politician, having succeeded in a coup. The safest choice is to denounce [character] publicly and to have him executed, strengthening your legitimacy. It might be better in the long term, however, to let [character]'s considerable skill at intrigue serve you instead.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Agent Missions

options.text: I will task [character] with an Insurrection or Treachery Mission in [city]!

events.text: [character] is now your Agent in [city]! As a dedicated Agent, he can perform Insurrection and Treachery Missions and will siphon off a percentage of the City's Yields, depending on the Ratings of [character]. (For example, his Wisdom will determine how much Science he will gather.) You can choose Agent Missions to perform from the Agent Character's Panel, the Spymaster Character's Panel, or even directly from the City in question by clicking the Agent icon(AGENT_HIGHLIGHTED) button beneath the City Banner.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Ambassador Missions

options.text: I will use my Ambassador for diplomatic missions!

events.text: You can use your Ambassador to conduct diplomatic Missions. Just select the portrait of your Ambassador in the top right, and you will see their available actions in the panel below. An Ambassador can make Peace with Nation and Tribe, form a Trade Mission, offer and demand Tribute, and more!

events.author: Gabe Campbell

options.text: I will try to keep my Family happy by accounting for the needs and desires of their Family Class.

events.text: Family have Family Class that determine what Laws, Luxury, and other conditions keep them happy. <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_FAMILY_LANDOWNERS>Landowners, like the angry [family], need land of course, so they want to have the most Cities of any of your Family, and they are especially displeased by having the fewest. Their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury like Olive and Honey. Always in need of labor for their fields, Landowners are pleased by the Serfdom Law.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_CHAMPIONS>The [family] are angry with you. They are Champions, so they like to fight, and their opinion of you will improve if they have the largest military of all your Family. Likewise, they will feel insulted if given the fewest military units. Their opinion of you will also increase with access to Luxury like Wine and Dye. Champions are pleased by the Volunteers Law.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_STATESMEN>Statesmen, like the angry [family], are of course concerned with matters of state and public opinion, and cast a wary eye on unmarried Leaders. They also seek advancement for themselves, and are dismayed by a Leader who does not share power by appointing Council Members. Their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury like Pearl and Wine. Statesmen are pleased by the adoption of a Constitution.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_PATRONS>Patrons, like the angry [family], are especially impressed by building Wonders. Their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury like Gem and Incense. Patrons are also pleased by the Calligraphy Law.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_CLERICS>Clerics, like the angry [family], want nothing more than to spread their faith. They are especially pleased by Holy City, but displeased when ruling over a City without a Religion. Their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury like Incense and Lavender. Enacting Divine Rule will also improve their opinion of you.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_SAGES>Sages, like the angry [family], look down on leaders with Tribal spouses, and they especially like if their cities contain the most Specialist. Their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury like Salt and Lavender. Sages are also pleased by the law Philosophy Law.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_TRADERS>Traders, such as the angry [family], will like you more if you keep their Cities connected, but are displeased by damaged Cities. It's bad for business. Their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury like Olive and Pearl. Traders are naturally pleased by the Trade League and Monetary Reform Laws.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_ARTISANS>Artisans, like the angry [family], can't stand interruptions in production, and so they are particularly distressed by pillaged Improvement in their territories. Their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury, especially Gem and Dye. Artisans are also pleased by the Guilds Law.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_RIDERS>Riders, like the angry [family], dislike you marrying foriegn spouses, but their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury like Fur and Salt. Riders are also pleased by more General belonging to their family, and the Vassalage Law.<p=SUBJECT_FAMILY_HUNTERS>Hunters, like the angry [family], are upset by hostile Tribe units in their territory, and their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury like Fur and Honey. Hunters are also pleased by the Exploration Law.<else>Artisans are particularly distressed by pillaged Improvement in their territories. Their opinion of you will improve with access to Luxury, especially Gem and Dye. Artisans are also pleased by the Guilds Law.<end> If the [family] remain angry with you, rebel Units may begin spawning in their Cities!

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Appoint Ambassador

options.text: I will appoint [character] as Ambassador, so that I may conduct diplomacy!
I will find a better candidate.

events.text: If you have researched the Aristocracy technology and you have an available candidate on your court with the Orator Archetype, Diplomat Archetype, or Commander Archetype Archetype, then you may appoint Ambassador using the glowing scroll icon icon(COUNCIL_AMBASSADOR) in the top right of the screen.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Appoint Chancellor

options.text: I will appoint [character] as Chancellor to help manage my realm!
I will find a better candidate.

events.text: If you have researched the Spoked Wheel technology and you have an available candidate on your court with the Zealot Archetype, Judge Archetype, or Builder Archetype Archetype, then you may appoint Chancellor using the glowing quill pen icon icon(COUNCIL_CHANCELLOR) in the top right of the screen.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Appoint Spymaster

options.text: I will appoint [character] as Spymaster, so that I can engage in some skulduggery!
I will find a better candidate.

events.text: If you have researched the Portcullis technology and you have an available candidate on your court with the Tactician Archetype, Schemer Archetype, or Scholar Archetype Archetype, then you may appoint Spymaster using the glowing eye icon icon(COUNCIL_SPYMASTER) in the top right of the screen.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Builder Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Builder Archetype Archetype. A Trait Builder Archetype can add Urban Tiles, and have multiple Worker work on a single Improvement. They also reduce the production time for Worker in all Cities by 50%.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Chancellor Missions

options.text: I will send my Chancellor on important missions!

events.text: You can use your Chancellor to help manage your realm with special Missions. Just select the portrait of your Chancellor in the top right, and you will see their available actions in the panel below. A Chancellor can give Family Gift to improve relations with your powerful Family, lower Discontent with Pacify City, and even Imprison troublesome Characters!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Civics Deficit

options.text: I will manage the nation's Civics income and stockpile!

events.text: Your nation is experiencing a Civics deficit! Courtier and Royal with low Charisma can drain your Civics, and cities working on new Project and Specialist will not add their Civics yield to the national pool. If Civics income is negative and the stockpile is empty, cities will be automatically switched to Council Project, which increase a city's civics output. To gain more Civics, consider switching some cities away from Project and Specialist production, and improving Opinion Character with Courtier and Royal whose Charisma is impacting Civics income.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Tutorial: Clergy

options.text: I will use [character] to improve religious relations and quell religious dissent!
I will remember this for the future!

events.text: As the various gods spread through [rival], so do the people who claim to serve and interpret the divine. There are different Clergy characters for different religions, whether pagan Clergy Pagan Assyria, Clergy Zoroastrian, Clergy Jewish, Clergy Christian, or Clergy Manichaean. Giving Clergy characters a job in your court will improve their religion’s opinion of you, and they can also quell Religious Dissent for their particular religion. The head of a religion can make a character of your choosing a member of the clergy through the Make Clergy mission.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Commander Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Commander Archetype Archetype. Idle Units receive an additional +10 XP/Turn under a Trait Commander Archetype, and Infantry Units an additional <color=#e3c08c><link="HELP_LINK,HELP_DEFENSE">+int(STRENGTH_MULTIPLIER)% icon(DEFENSE)</link></color>. As a General, a Trait Commander Archetype grants <color=#e3c08c><link="HELP_LINK,HELP_UNIT_STRENGTH">+20% icon(ATTACKDEFENSE)</link></color> to Adjacent Units and, additionally, <color=#e3c08c><link="HELP_LINK,HELP_ATTACK_VALUE">+100% icon(ATTACK)</link></color> when Flanking.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Diplomat Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Diplomat Archetype Archetype. A Trait Diplomat Archetype receives a +60 boost to Opinion Character from all other leaders, are also the only Archetype of leader who can propose Alliances to tribes and nations.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Family Opinion

options.text: I will try to keep my Family happy so that they don't rebel!

events.text: One of your Family is Angry with you! Family opinion is influenced by the Discontent in their Cities and by player Event choices. Cities gain Discontent over time. You can reduce Discontent by connecting your Cities with Road, adopting a State Religion, building certain Improvement like Baths, and enacting certain Laws such as Divine Rule and Tolerance. If a Family is Angry with you, then Rebel Units may begin spawning in their Cities!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Food Shortage

options.text: I will manage the nation's Food income and stockpiles!

events.text: Your nation is experiencing a Food shortage! Cities and units can require Food as upkeep, and when the nation's stockpile reaches zero, Money is automatically spent to buy any Food needed for upkeep. To increase Food production, use Worker to construct Farm improvements around your cities.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Gambling

options.text: Kings make their own luck.

events.text: You, [character], now have the option to Gamble, to while away your time laying bets with nobility and the lowborn alike. As king, gambling can be a profitable endeavor, as your winnings are quickly recognized, and small debts are just as quickly forgotten. All the same, sometimes it is not coin but reputations that are at stake. To Gamble, choose the option from the action panel on the bottom left of the screen while your leader is selected.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Grand Vizier

options.text: I will think carefully who to grant such power.

events.text: The Grand Vizier is a special position with enormous powers of administration over your cities. Rising Star has the political power to take up the position, as does any sufficiently Power Hungry character. While you have a Grand Vizier in office, you will not be able to personally manage production in cities without Governor, and those characters eligible for the position are not the sort to resign such authority easily. On the other hand, a Grand Vizier can provide significant benefits to cities they manage. These benefits are based on the Grand Vizier's Rating and traits, just the same as for governors.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Hero Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Hero Archetype Archetype. A Trait Hero Archetype gains an additional +50 Training per Military Unit killed, allows all military units to Heal while pillaging, and as a General can Launch Offensive. Hero Archetype Characters also have higher Courage, which as a Leader causes their nation to produce more Training.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Hire Mercenaries

options.text: I will hire [tribe] Mercenary to bolster my forces!

events.text: As Carthage, you can hire Mercenary in exchange for Money from Tribe like the [tribe]. You may not hire Raiders. Mercenary have no associated Family and int(CONSUMPTION_MERCENARY_MODIFIER)% higher consumption costs. They cannot receive Promotion, but they can be Upgrade. They may only be led by a General from their own Ethnicity. To hire a Mercenary Unit, simply select a Tribal Unit that is not garrisoning a Tribal Site, and click the Hire Mercenary icon(HIRE_MERCENARY) button in the Unit Panel on the left.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Hold Court

options.text: Let us Hold Court in [rival].
I am too busy for that at the moment.

events.text: Hold Court Missions give you the chance to gain Civics at the cost of Training, and a few Orders. The mission may also recruit a new Courtier, or lead to follow up events. With a Judge Archetype Leader, you can Hold Court by clicking the gavel icon(MISSION_HOLD_COURT) button in the Action Panel on the top right, while your leader is selected. Will you start a Hold Court Mission?

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Hurry Production

options.text: I'll Hurry in my Cities if I need to!

events.text: Now that [city] has reached the Developing Culture Level, various options for Hurry in the City have become available. With the Developing (or higher) Culture Level alone, a City can Hurry at the cost of some Civics and Discontent. Other methods of Hurry are further enabled by certain Governor traits or Laws like Orthodoxy and Volunteers. These distinct means of Hurry cost resources other than Civics (although they all produce Discontent). For example, with the Holy War Law and a State Religion you can Hurry with Money. You can see the different options for Hurry in the City Panel underneath the current production in progress. Hurry can be expensive but can also save you in a tight spot!

events.author: Gabe Campbell/Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Imprison

options.text: Imprison [character]!
I don't wish to Imprison anyone at the moment.

events.text: A Chancellor can conduct an Imprison Mission, to jail troublesome characters within your nation at the cost of Training and Orders. Imprisoned characters cannot marry, have children, succeed to the throne, or have a job of any kind. An Imprison Mission is initiated by clicking the icon(MISSION_IMPRISON) Imprison button in the Action Panel on the right, while selecting your Chancellor, or the character you wish to Imprison.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Influence

options.text: Let me work my wiles on [character].
I am too busy for that at the moment.

events.text: Influence Missions give you the chance to improve another Character's Opinion Character of your leader, at the cost of a few Orders and some Money. They may also lead to follow up Events. You can conduct an Influence Mission by clicking the icon(MISSION_INFLUENCE) Influence button in the Action Panel on the right, while a Character other than your Leader is selected. Almost everyone, even leaders of other Nation and Tribe can be influenced!

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Inheritance

options.text: I will change my Succession Law if I want!

events.text: Now that you have a new Heir, [character], it's time to learn about Succession Law! On the left side of the top bar, you can open the Inheritance Screen with the Crown icon(INHERITANCE_Normal) button. The Inheritance Screen will show your current Succession. If you click the Change Law button, you can see who the new Heirs would be, depending on which Succession Law you select to preview. You can choose different schemes, like Ultimogeniture or Seniority, based on your preference.

events.author: Gabe Campbell/Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Intercession

options.text: Have [character] intercede with [character] on my behalf.
I am too busy for that at the moment.

events.text: Intercession Religion and Intercession Family Missions let Pleased Family or Religion Heads in your nation speak to another Character on your behalf. At the cost of Orders and Money, Opinion Character can be improved, and they can also lead to follow up events. You can conduct these missions by selecting the character you wish to target (or, the Family or Religion Head) and then clicking the icon(MISSION_INTERCESSION) Intercession button in the top right Action Panel. Religion Heads can intercede with almost anyone of that religion, even other leaders, while Family heads can intercede with members of that family.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Iron Shortage

options.text: I will manage the nation's Iron income and stockpiles!

events.text: Your nation is experiencing an Iron shortage! Military units and cities can require Iron as upkeep, and when the nation's stockpile reaches zero, Money is automatically spent to buy any Iron needed for upkeep. To increase Iron production, use Worker to construct Mine improvements around your cities.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Judge Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Judge Archetype Archetype. A Trait Judge Archetype may switch laws for a low flat cost of 100 Civics, and can Upgrade Improvements. They can also conduct Hold Court Missions.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Luxury

options.text: I will send [resource] to the [family] now!
I will send Luxury to Family, Cities, and Tribe at my convenience later.

events.text: Luxury are special Resources (like Gem or Dye) that can be traded to other Nation, Tribe and Family in exchange for an Opinion boost. Certain Family Class even have favorite Luxury that they especially desire! In order to acquire a Luxury, you must build the correct Improvement on that Resource, and the Improvement must be augmented with a Specialist. Luxury can be sent to the desired target with the Manage Luxuries icon(LuxuryUp) button on the Action Panel, while a Nation, Tribe, or Family is selected, or in the bottom left of the City Screen for Cities. You may currently send [resource] to the [family], if you so desire! Or, you may wait and send this Luxury somewhere else at your convenience. To send the same type of a Luxury to multiple targets, you must have multiple sources of it.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Maximum Civics Stockpile

options.text: I will use my Civics to maximum effect!

events.text: Your national stockpile of Civics has reached 2,000! This is the maximum amount of Civics that can be stored, with any excess being automatically converted to Science at a rate of int(CIVICS_PER_SCIENCE):1. To make full use of your Civics, consider using them to enact Laws, Hurry in cities with Developing Culture or better, or appoint Councilor and send them on important missions.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Maximum Training Stockpile

options.text: I will use my Training to maximum effect!

events.text: Your national stockpile of Training has reached 2,000! This is the maximum amount of Training that can be stored, with any excess being automatically converted to Orders at a rate of int(TRAINING_PER_ORDER):1. To leverage your Training into a stronger military, consider using it to appoint new General and upgrade military units with new Promotion. You can also buy Orders with Training at any time by clicking the icon(YIELD_ORDERS) icon near the leader portrait.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Money Deficit

options.text: I will manage the nation's Money income and stockpiles!

events.text: Your nation is experiencing a Money deficit! Cities, Courtier and Royal can all cost Money as upkeep. When the nation's Money stockpile reaches zero, Food, Iron, Stone and Wood will be sold to pay upkeep, based on which resource has the highest price and rate of production. To generate more money, consider using Worker to build Hamlet and keeping an eye on the Discipline of important characters.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Orator Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is an Orator Archetype Archetype. An Trait Orator Archetype receives a +40 Opinion Religion from all Religions and can Recruit Mercenary icon(RECRUIT_MERCENARY) with icon(YIELD_LEGITIMACY)Legitimacy. They also get +1 Orders a Year per Friendly City.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Orders

options.text: I'll have to consider how to use my Orders carefully each turn!

events.text: Orders are an important feature of Old World. Units can move multiple times each turn, but each move consumes one Orders. Other actions, such as attacking or building, also consume Orders. Your remaining Orders can be seen in the lower left corner of your screen. We recommend that you first select your Worker, so that you may begin to improve your land before you spend all of your Orders for the turn.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Rally the Troops

options.text: I am feeling invigorated already! Let's go on a Mission to Rally Troops.
No, I am too busy for that at the moment.

events.text: In times of war like these, the troops like to hear encouragement from their leader. A rousing speech on the glories of [rival], and the unmatched courage of her fighting men, would improve morale. You can conduct a Rally Troops Mission by clicking the icon(MISSION_RALLY_TROOPS) button in the Action Panel on the top right, while your Leader is selected. Rally Troops Missions give you the chance to gain Training at the cost of Civics, and a few Orders. They may also lead to follow up events. Will you go out on a Rally Troops Mission?

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Recruit Mercenaries

options.text: I will recruit [tribe] Mercenary to bolster my forces!

events.text: You have an Orator Archetype Leader, and you've already met your first Tribe, the [tribe]. Any nation with an Orator Archetype Leader may recruit Tribal Mercenary at the cost of some icon(YIELD_LEGITIMACY)Legitimacy. You may not hire Raiders. Mercenary have no associated Family and int(CONSUMPTION_MERCENARY_MODIFIER)% higher consumption costs. They cannot receive Promotion, but they can be Upgrade. They may only be led by a General from their own Ethnicity. To recruit a Mercenary Unit, simply select a Tribal Unit that is not garrisoning a Tribal Site, and click the Recruit Mercenary icon(RECRUIT_MERCENARY) button in the Unit Panel on the left.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Tutorial: Religious Dissent

outcomes.label: Tutorial Religious Dissent Clergy Option 0 Z
Tutorial Religious Dissent Clergy Option 0 J
Tutorial Religious Dissent Clergy Option 0 C
Tutorial Religious Dissent Clergy Option 0 M

options.text: We will deal with this later!

events.text: Religious Dissent has broken out in [city]! This project is added through events and there is a chance for it to appear when a religion in your nation is upset with you. As well as adding the chance for rebels, it increases the rate of training. Religious Dissent can be removed from cities by Clergy characters of the same religion, such as [character].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Tutorial: Religious Dissent

options.text: I will use clergy characters to quell this religious dissent!

events.text: Religious Dissent has broken out in [city]! This project is added through events and there is a chance for it to appear when a religion in your nation is upset with you. As well as adding the chance for rebels, it will stop the random spread of religions in the city. Religious Dissent can be removed from cities by Clergy characters of the same religion, who can be made by the religion head’s Make Clergy mission.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Rural Yields

options.text: I will build more Farm and Mine!

events.text: The Rural Yields are Food, Iron, Stone, and Wood. They are primarily drawn from rural Improvement and collect in the Global stockpile. You can spend Money to purchase Rural Yields directly from the top bar where it shows your current stockpile. The primary source of Food is Farm, which are most fruitful next to Fresh Water and on Lush Terrain. Food is needed to feed your Population and to produce new Settler. The primary source of Iron is Mine, which are most productive on Ore and Hill. Iron is needed to produce many types of Military Units, including Warrior and Axeman. The primary source of Stone is Quarry, which are most productive on Marble, on Arid Terrain, and when adjacent to Mountain. Stone is needed primarily to build Improvement like Shrine and City Project such as Walls. The Forestry Tech enables the construction of Lumbermill on Trees to produce Wood. Worker can also cut down Trees with the icon(REMOVE_TREES) Button in the Actions panel. Wood is needed to build City Improvement like Range, Military Units like Archer, and Ship Units like Bireme.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Schemer Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Schemer Archetype Archetype. A Trait Schemer Archetype can conduct Adopt Missions and buy Orders with icon(YIELD_LEGITIMACY)Legitimacy. They also get +1 Orders a Year per War, a 10% bonus to Agent yields, and their Scout are Invisible.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Scholar Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Scholar Archetype Archetype. A Trait Scholar Archetype can conduct Tutor Scholar Missions and Redraw Technology choices. They also get extra Science per Archive Project.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Skipping Families

options.text: A one-family nation will become unstable with time.

events.text: Your nation has grown to three cities and all three are controlled by the [family] family. While it is possible to skip additional families, Discontent increases from doing so. Skipping a family may sometimes provide a temporary advantage but it should not be a long-term plan - your nation will be much easier to manage if you use all the available families.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Specialist

options.text: I will recruit some Specialist to boost my production!

events.text: A Specialist can be recruited from the City Screen by clicking the icon(specialist_border) button on an Improvement so long as you have an available Citizen. Although Improvement are already productive on their own, a Specialist can boost their yields. Luxury are special resources that you acquire by adding a Rural Specialist to an Improvement on the correct Tile. For example, you access Gem by adding a Miner Specialist to a Mine Improvement on a Gem Tile. Urban Specialist, like Acolyte and Officer, can be trained to higher levels for further yield boosts.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Spymaster Missions

options.text: I will use my Spymaster for secret missions!

events.text: You can use your Spymaster to conduct secret Missions! Just select the portrait of your Spymaster in the top right, and you will see their available actions in the panel below. Spymaster can execute missions like Infiltrate, Steal Research, Assassinate, and more!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Stone Shortage

options.text: I will manage the nation's Stone income and stockpiles!

events.text: Your nation is experiencing a Stone shortage! Cities, Improvement and units can require Stone as upkeep, and when the nation's stockpile reaches zero, Money is automatically spent to buy any Stone needed for upkeep. To increase Stone production, research Stonecutting and use Worker to construct Quarry improvements around your cities.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Stressed

options.text: I'll deal with the pressure.

events.text: You, [character], have become Stressed. Being stressed reduces your ability to govern and command, and in particular lowers your income of Science, Civics, and Money, and prevents using Influence. How long you spend stressed can be reduced if you Revel. Revelry costs Money, and can have other side effects, but it will usually do the trick! To Revel, choose the option from the action panel on the bottom left of the screen while your leader is selected.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Surplus Food

options.text: I will use my Food stockpile to maximum effect!

events.text: A surplus of Food has accumulated in your nation's stockpiles. Food can be used to train Settler and some new Specialist and Mounted units. It is also spent as upkeep to feed your units and your cities as they grow. Excess Food can be sold for Money, which can in turn buy Iron, Stone, or Wood.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Surplus Iron

options.text: I will use my Iron stockpile to maximum effect!

events.text: A surplus of Iron has accumulated in your nation's stockpiles. Iron is used for the training and upkeep of many military units, like Warrior, and for construction of some improvements, like Quarry. Excess Iron can be sold for Money, which can in turn buy Food, Stone, or Wood.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Surplus Stone

options.text: I will use my Stone stockpile to maximum effect!

events.text: A surplus of Stone has accumulated in your nation's stockpiles. Stone is used for the construction of Road, many advanced Improvement, and is an essential component for Wonder. Excess Stone can be sold for Money, which can in turn buy Food, Iron, or Wood.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Surplus Wood

options.text: I will use my Wood stockpile to maximum effect!

events.text: A surplus of Wood has accumulated in your nation's stockpiles. Wood is used for the construction of many Improvement and some military units, such as Archer and Bireme. Excess Wood can be sold for Money, which can in turn buy Food, Iron, or Stone.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Tactician Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Tactician Archetype Archetype. A Trait Tactician Archetype increases the Vision Range of your Units by 2, and allows Ranged Units to be Hidden in neutral as well as friendly Trees. As a General, a Trait Tactician Archetype Stun their targets.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Take the Field

options.text: Yes, I belong on the field of battle.
No, I am needed in the capital.

events.text: A Character can be assigned as a General to a Unit, contributing their Unique bonuses to the Unit. Assign a General by selecting a Unit and then clicking the Add General icon(JOB_GENERAL) button in the Action Panel on the left. A General (with the exception of the Leader) cannot be from a different Family from that of the Unit. Our [unit] unit has been hard at work training for battle, and they are ready for leadership. Will you take the role of General and lead them?

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Tooltips

options.text: I will lock tooltips in place with hotkey(HOTKEY_FREEZE_TOOLTIP)+Click to discover more information!

events.text: The nested tooltip system in Old World allows windows to persist as you link from one to another. Simply hold hotkey(HOTKEY_FREEZE_TOOLTIP) while hovering over a link and move the mouse cursor into the tooltip and click, or click the link with the Middle Mouse Button, to lock the new window in place. This lets you continue to view a window while opening more links, even if you move the cursor off of the window altogether. Try it out on this Unit link: Spearman. Press the ESC key, or click away from all tooltip windows, to make them disappear after they are locked.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Training Deficit

options.text: I will manage the nation's Training income and stockpile!

events.text: Your nation is experiencing a Training deficit! Courtier and Royal with low Courage can drain your Training, and military units consume Training in upkeep. If Training income is negative and the stockpile is empty, cities will be automatically switched to Council Project, which increase a city's training output. To gain more Training, consider switching some cities away from military unit production, and improving Opinion Character with Courtier and Royal whose Courage is impacting Training income.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Upgrade Mercenaries

options.text: I will upgrade Mercenary to make them stronger!

events.text: As Carthage, you now have a hired Mercenary unit in your territory. These Tribal units start out fairly weak, but they can be Upgrade to stronger versions. Unlike regular units, it only costs Training to Upgrade tribal units, letting [rival] build a capable army without expending other resources.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tutorial: Wood Shortage

options.text: I will manage the nation's Wood income and stockpiles!

events.text: Your nation is experiencing a Wood shortage! Improvement, cities and units can require Wood as upkeep, and when the nation's stockpile reaches zero, Money is automatically spent to buy any Wood needed for upkeep. More Wood can be gained by sending Worker to chop down Trees near cities. To increase passive Wood production, research Forestry and use Worker to construct Lumbermill improvements.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Tutorial: Zealot Archetype Archetype

options.text: I will make the best use of my Leader based on their Archetype!

events.text: Your Leader [character] is a Zealot Archetype Archetype. A Trait Zealot Archetype adds +1 to the Fatigue limit of your Units, and can Hurry with Training. As a General, a Trait Zealot Archetype may use the ability Enlist to recruit enemy units.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Unchecked

options.text: We must get a man inside to deal with [character].
Order military officers to divert resources to [city].
I will go and treat with [character] in person.

events.text: Left alone to strengthen his hold on [city], [character]'s power has gone unchecked for years. It appears he is no longer satisfied with simply ruling a city. At [character]'s urging, citizens in [city] have begun rising up against royal forces. This aggression will only spread.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Unchecked Power

options.text: I see. You have thought of everything, I suppose.
I would sooner die than aid you traitors.

events.text: The captain of the guard stands conspicuously still and refuses to meet your eyes as you call for [character] and [character] to be removed from the audience. [character] smiles. "I think you will find we have support from across divided classes and families of [rival]. But this needn't be acrimonious. True, we shall rule... but you could yet have a place by the throne."

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Unhappy Sibling

options.text: Provide [character] with whatever he needs.
We cannot waste resources on my ungrateful siblings.

events.text: A careful investigation reveals that [character] was never plotting to betray you, but was simply unhappy in your shadow. He believes that his contributions often go overlooked. Perhaps there is something we can do for [character].

events.author: Solver
events.name: Unholy Murder

options.text: My reign is over, but it is Aten who will judge me.

events.text: As you conclude the evening prayers in your private chambers, [character] barges in without warning, followed by shapes you recognize, after a brief confusion, as elder [family]. Even as [character] raises his dagger, they're already discussing how to restore Egypt to glory after what you did to the land.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Unrequited

options.text: Sit with [character] and listen.
Send condolences to [rival].
Do nothing.

events.text: The court receives sad news from [rival]. [character], heir to the [rival] throne, has taken his own life. In a final message, he lamented his unrequited passion for [character], a love he was forbidden to pursue. Struck by this tragedy, [character] retreats into his quarters.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Usurped!

options.text: It was nice while it lasted.

events.text: You have ignored the signs. You have overlooked the threats. Chaos erupts, as the personal guards of [character] storm into the court and take you prisoner. It seems that the [family] Family has been plotting with [rival] all along. Now, they plan to replace you with [character] on the throne.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Vassal Ceremony

options.text: We must accept this great honor.
Finance it only, as a compromise.
No, the [family] must remember their place.

events.text: To cement our close ties, the [family] family have invited us to finance and preside over their most sacred ceremony. This is a great honor, reserved only for [family] nobles, which makes it a blatant act of favoritism. Do we accept?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Vassal Feast

options.text: If we must, to keep them happy.
The [family] have overreached this time.

events.text: The entitled [family] family has become bolder in their requests. They are hosting a celebratory feast in honor of their ancestral founder, and have asked us to supply food and pay for entertainment. Such a request is not custom. How shall we respond?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Vested Interest

options.text: Send delegations of guards to protect the coast.
The fleet will deal with these so-called pirates.
See if any of the pirates are willing to strike a deal.

events.text: The Trade Winds in [city] have helped the merchants of the city to prosper. Even a single ship laden with luxuries and riches from foreign lands can set up an investor for life. However, such journeys are not without danger. Pirates roam the shores and prey on the ships they find. To combat this, merchants are paying private guards and archers to protect the ships.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Vicious Rumors

options.text: I support the [family] family.
I stand with the [family].
Take the gifts, but support neither family.
I wish to stay out these endless squabbles!

events.text: Unsurprisingly, two of your vassal families are squabbling. The [family] family accuses the [family] of spreading vicious rumors about them. When confronted, the [family] elders claim to know nothing about such slander. Each family comes to you with a gift, asking for support. What do we tell them?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Victorious Champion

options.text: Accept their Tribute.
Freedom from [rival] will cost you.
[rival] must pay for this reckless display.

events.text: After a brutal and suspenseful fight, your champion claims victory over his [rival] opponent. The dead man's companions cannot conceal their great displeasure. "We are willing to renegotiate the terms of our offer." What shall we tell them?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Victorious!

options.text: Destiny guides my hand.

events.text: You have emerged victorious from your royal duel with [character]. As expiation for their hostility, the [rival] offer their prayers. Peace persists.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Ward No Longer

options.text: I stand by [character], as if he were my own blood.
He is a part of the family, although will remain unrecognized by the succession.

events.text: Your ward [character] has grown up as a part of your family. As he reaches adulthood the question looms, what future role will the young scion play in your court?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Washtub Philosopher

options.text: A delegation will bring him back to the capital.
I do not want to get involved in his madness.
Several months at the temple will clear his head.

events.text: After years of interesting behavior, [character], the famous ascetic, retreats even further into eccentricity and isolation. He takes up residence inside an abandoned washtub in the center of [city]. Many in the nobility seem vexed by the presence of [character], but he is quite popular among the poor and indigent.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Weakness Shown

options.text: [character] has made a grave mistake.

events.text: The court waits with baited breath for word of [character] diplomatic expedition to [tribe] lands. This waiting is finally answered by the return of [character] severed head.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Whispers of Betrayal

options.text: We must stay our hand to keep the peace.
Imprison the plotter immediately.
Make [character] disappear quietly.

events.text: [character]'s agents in the [family] family have overheard talk of plots against your life. These whispers of machinations against the throne name [character] as the lead conspirator. We should arrange for his removal. However, doing so will alienate the [family] Family. How shall we proceed?

events.author: Solver
events.name: Your Best Friend

options.text: He is to me what Patroclus was to Achilles.

events.text: Today is the day your childhood friend [character] completes his military education. Being of similar age, you have been together for much of your upbringing, often attending the same lessons and spending many spare evenings together sparring, discussing the Iliad or just talking about the things boys have talked about since ancient times. [character] beams as you, in your capacity as King, congratulate him on his graduation. Immediately, [character] asks to serve you directly, a request you knew would come and that he knows you want to hear. There is nobody you would rather fight along with, nobody you could ever trust more than you trust [character]. Whatever great battles lie ahead of you, you know what history will describe [character] and [character] as two halves of the army.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Your Coup to Leave

options.text: Politics is no place for passion.

events.text: It is quiet, there is no bloodshed, no grand announcements. But sure as the seasons turn, [character] and [character] find themselves shut out of decisions, carefully steered to far off estates, and eventually even pressured out of ceremonial roles. The houses of [family] and [family] carry on as before, and it is only those with front row seats who carry knowledge of the little plot.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Your Husband's Wedding

options.text: Why would it matter? He is dead to me.
Congratulate the happy couple!
Send him the head of his favorite servant. As a gift!

events.text: We wish to inform you of upsetting news before you hear it through courtly gossip. Your former husband, [character], has fallen in love with the powerful [character] of [rival]. The two have wed in a grand ceremony in the courtyard of the [city] palace. We hope and pray this development does not affect our standing with the [rival].

events.author: Solver
events.name: Your Time Has Come

options.text: [rival] is about to see what I can do!

events.text: [rival] finds itself at war for the first time under your leadership. Historians will one day judge whether the conflict with [rival] was inevitable or not but you know that a victory now will ensure future historians take the right point of view. One of the most memorable conversations you've had about warfare with your father was on the subject of elephants. The idea of using these fearsome beasts to strike terror into the enemy has long fascinated you. With elephants and more traditional troops as well, you can make a name for yourself after defeating [rival].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Zoroastrian Dissent

options.text: Prepare the guards for any unrest.
Seek to appease the local [religion] leaders.
Take no action, for now.

events.text: [religion] discontent has spilled onto the streets of [city], Unhappy with your rule, the local are leading the faithful in attacks on the guards and encouraging resistance against the crown.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character]

options.text: I shall work with [character], at least for now.

outcomes.label: The Vizier Support Or Scheme Option 1 Main
The Vizier Support Or Scheme Option 1 Fallback

options.text: [character] power must be... curtailed.

events.text: Local ministers from [city] to [city] now take their orders from your Grand Vizier, rather than from your throne room. Do you trust [character] competence with these decisions? Can his loyalty be certain? You could, of course, Scheme Against Rival at any time to attempt to wrest back control.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Reforms

options.text: Even [character] opponents are unhappy at the complete disarray he has left.

events.text: With [character] out of power, his reforms program has ground to chaotic halt.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Returns

options.text: My, how forward. You know what, why not, I can always use another husband.

events.text: [character], the [tribe] warlord who laid claim to the lands of [city], returns to court with a glint in his eye. "The lands of [city] remain in your cruel [rival] clutches, and so, alas, does my heart. If we cannot wed, the path of the sword is the only path that I can see."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Unchecked
events.text: [tribe] power continues to rise, as enterprising warriors test [rival] defenses.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Was Ready

options.text: I shall not underestimate [character] again.

events.text: [character] did not make it far into [tribe] lands. At every turn, he and his band were outmaneuvered, ambushed, and picked to pieces. He limps back to [city], a broken man, with [tribe] warriors no doubt hot on the heels.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [character] and [character]

options.text: An example must be made. Execute them all.
Refuse to punish those that stood against you.

events.text: [character] returns to the city in triumph. People line the streets to watch the procession and to catch a glimpse of the famous rebel, [character], walking behind [character] in chains. The threat of war is over, but it is still to be decided what should be done with the remaining rebels. [character] looks up and behind those eyes you see a lifetime of suffering, of pain and grief beyond that which any person should have to endure.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [character] at the Gates

options.text: It is time to end these rebellions once and for all!
[rival] will never again enslave others.

events.text: [character] stands before the gates of our capital. “Your lies and tricks will not work on us. We will never surrender!” At his cry, the thousands of rebels shout out in unison, their anger shaking the very buildings. At last it has come to a fight. [character]’s gambit failed and your scouts report seeing his body being carried as a prize by rebels. There is only one thing left that could quell the tide - offering total emancipation, pardoning the rebels and freeing all of the slaves of [rival].

events.author: Solver
events.name: [character]'s Offer

options.text: Welcome, old friend!

events.text: As you finish another training session and dismount Bucephalus, you find [character] waiting for you. You know the man well - he served in the army with your father and helped you be named the successor to the throne. It has been some time since you last saw [character] and rumors persist of a falling out between him and your mother. [character] has come with a simple message. He wishes to serve on your court as a military advisor, as he once served your father. Even though [character] is growing older, his experience will still be useful and his loyalty to you is beyond question.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: [city] Returns

options.text: We welcome back [city] with celebrations!

events.text: After much consideration, the leaders of [rival] have decided to return the city of [city] to us, as a token of good faith. Our people will not soon forget this.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: [city] Returns

options.text: We welcome back [city] with celebrations!

events.text: Chieftains of the conquering [tribe] Tribe send a message to the court, informing us that they will return the city of [city] to [rival]. These [tribe] have our gratitude.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: [family] displeasure

options.text: I care little for either of you.
Perhaps I can show [character] more favor.

events.text: [character] has come before you to inform you that he is deeply upset with your treatment of [character]. By disparaging him, [character] feels you insult the [family].

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: [family] influence

options.text: I treasure [character] as I do the [family].

events.text: The [family] family is pleased that you clearly favor [character], as this adds to their power and influence throughout [rival]. “When you elevate [character] above all others, so do you elevate the [family]!”

events.author: Solver
events.name: [religion] Goodwill

options.text: A mind-opening spirit travel session would be just right.
I would like to be presented with the precious fuel that kindles holy fires.
Clear and public recognition of me as a patron of [religion] is the best choice.

events.text: You have become known as a patron of [religion] among its followers. The religion's leaders and regular followers alike hold you in high regard. As a sign of good will and respect, the magi propose blessings and a ceremony in your honor. How would you like to be honored?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [religion] Intrigue

options.text: What a disappointment.
No, this is just the start.

events.text: A servant wakes you late in the night with news that [character] has taken ill, and is close to death. Hurrying to his side, you are surprised to find [character] standing over the barely breathing body. [character] speaks to you in a soft voice, unnoticed by the grieving family, eyes never leaving [character]. “What a shame to see a promising life cut so short, isn’t it? Especially a faithful supporter of [religion] with such… potential.” He turns to leave. The sad smile never leaves his lips, but the cold eyes send a different message: this is what happens when you scheme against [character].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [religion] Intrigue

options.text: Beg forgiveness for your actions.
Refuse to apologize.
Claim that is was a ploy by your enemies to sow discord between you.

events.text: It seems that [character] has learned of your plans to replace him as the Head of [religion] with [character]. A furious message demands an explanation of why he shouldn’t reveal this and turn the priesthood against you.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [religion] Intrigue

options.text: What a disappointment.

events.text: Your attempts to install [character] as the head of [religion] have been cut short by his untimely death.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [religion] Intrigue

options.text: Kill [character].
Publicly disgrace him.
Not like this, we will wait for a better opportunity.
No, this has gone too far.

events.text: Your Spymaster [character] brings news that his agents have managed to infiltrate the household of [character]. If you are able to shore up support for [character] from among the, then this could be the perfect opportunity to put your chosen candidate at the head of [religion]. [character] objects to the use of violence and suggests causing a scandal would be as effective in removing [character]. It would be merciful to leave him alive, but it leaves an enemy with a grudge out in the world. What do you command?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [religion] Intrigue

options.text: Give the go-ahead.
Not like this, we will wait for a better opportunity.
No, enough is enough.

events.text: An opportunity has arisen to place [character] as the head of [religion], but it is not a pleasant one. [character] has informed you that [character] is going to be visiting your capital shortly, bringing only a paltry few guards. He suggests that your troops could overwhelm [character]’s men, and forcibly install [character] in his place. The plan is effective, although hardly subtle, and will likely see a lot of [religion] blood spilled. Will you go through with it?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [religion] Intrigue

options.text: Force through laws that rule [character] unfit to lead.
Pay off the remaining to shore up support.
Use the military to covertly enforce a transition.
No, this has gone too far.

events.text: Your support amongst the worshipers of [religion] has been steadily growing with your recent actions, even eclipsing their love of [character]. A small sect of the have approached you declaring that they are willing to aid you however necessary. Support from within the religion changes things. With just a little push, this could be the perfect opportunity to install [character] as the head of [religion].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [religion] Intrigue

options.text: Refuse to be blackmailed.
Convince him that it’s all a misunderstanding.
Agree to drop the plans.

events.text: “I cannot allow this disgrace to!” [character] has heard rumors of your intent to replace [character] with [character] as the head of [religion] and is making sure to let his feelings be known. At the end of his protests [character] gives an ultimatum: Drop your plan or he will inform [character] of your intentions.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: [rival] Anger

options.text: Indeed.
Perhaps I can show [character] more favor.

events.text: An emissary from [rival] has come before you to express dismay over the treatment of [character]. “[character] is as much a diplomat as a spouse, by mistreating him you mistreat [rival]” the emissary proclaims!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [rival] Rules [rival], for Now

options.text: This could only ever end in war.

events.text: [character] arrives back in [city] by a circuitous route. You can only imagine the conversation between him and [character]. The results of that conversation, however, leave little ambiguity.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [rival] Rules [rival], for Now

options.text: This could only ever end in war.

events.text: The death of [character] does not go without notice. Hollow assurances of loyalty to [character] are for naught as the [rival] war machine shifts gears.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: [tribe] Anger

options.text: Indeed.
Perhaps I can show [character] more favor.

events.text: An envoy has arrived from the [tribe] to express their anger over [character] falling from your favor. “Your marriage was meant to bind our people together. By snubbing [character], so too do you snub [tribe],” the envoy announces!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [tribe] Disarray
events.text: [character] and his handpicked band of fighters cut a swathe of chaos through [tribe] lands, culminating in an ambush of [character] himself. The band returns with fame, stories, and plunder in equal measure.
